signals.topic: Tool calling fails across multiple API providers and models due to JSON output/parsing errors
signals.summary: When agents call tools via OpenAI-compatible APIs (DashScope, vllm, Ali OpenAI interface), the request fails with errors like 'messages must contain the word json' (400), TypeError, or parsing failures. This blocks the core tool-use workflow.
signals.review_reason: 3条issue均指向同一根因：模型返回的tool_call相关输出（JSON格式、结束标签、流式拼接）在agentscope解析层失败，导致核心工具调用流程完全阻断。#1360 表现为任务卡死，#1354 表现为API 400报错且需手动恢复，#1351 表现为边界情况参数错配。用户无法正常使用agent的工具调用能力，属于高频主流程阻断。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: 我使用阿里兼容的openai接口调用工具报错
source_issues.evidence: API调用报400错误，'messages must contain the word json' for response_format=json_object；工具调用超出次数后必须清除消息才能恢复，主流程阻断

source_issues.title: [Bug]:消息遇到</tool_call>任务会卡主
source_issues.evidence: 模型返回包含</tool_call>时任务完全卡住，无任何后续输出，主流程完全阻断

source_issues.title: [Bug]: An edge case of JSON string repair for tool callings
source_issues.evidence: JSON修复逻辑存在边界情况：流式输出时若中间修复结果长度大于最终结果长度，不完整数据会被当作最终工具参数，导致工具调用失败

signals.topic: ReActAgent produces inconsistent outputs between thinking enabled and disabled modes
signals.summary: When using enable_thinking: False vs True in ReActAgent, the agent produces completely different (and sometimes wrong) outputs. Without thinking, the agent may hallucinate unrelated content. This affects reliability of agent responses.
aliases: 思考模式开关输出不一致
thinking模式差异导致结果不同
signals.review_reason: 两条issue均反映agent输出质量在有无thinking模式时存在显著差异。#1376直接体现thinking开关导致结果不同；#1366虽包含toolkit因素但同样展示agent在推理不足时的幻觉问题。count=2但根因混合（框架行为+模型能力），降为P2边缘项。

source_issues.title: [Bug]:智能体关闭思考模式和不关闭场景下输出结果不一致
source_issues.evidence: 同一ReActAgent配置，仅改变enable_thinking开关，输出结果完全不同。用户明确表示只有开启思考时结果才是期望的，关闭思考后结果错误但原因不明

source_issues.title: [Bug]:reactagent不加toolkit时乱回答
source_issues.evidence: ReActAgent不加载toolkit时，模型产生幻觉输出（把用户输入"你好"理解为"rollers"），回复完全错误。虽然enable_thinking=False时也收到WARNING，但核心问题是agent无工具时质量严重下降

signals.topic: Knowledge retrieval crashes with TypeError when document metadata contains extra fields like 'filename'
signals.summary: When retrieving from the knowledge base after adding custom metadata fields (e.g., 'filename') to documents, the retrieve() call crashes with TypeError: DocMetadata got an unexpected keyword argument. This blocks the knowledge retrieval feature entirely.
signals.review_reason: 用户添加自定义元数据是合理需求，但agentscope的DocMetadata模型不接纳额外字段导致整个retrieve流程崩溃。这不是边缘场景——为知识库文档附加额外属性是常见做法，崩溃直接导致知识检索功能不可用。

source_issues.title: [Bug]:执行knowledge.retrieve搜索方法，报错got an unexpected keyword argument 'filename'
source_issues.evidence: 用户给文档添加filename元数据后，执行knowledge.retrieve()立即抛出TypeError: DocMetadata.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'filename'，位于_qdrant_store.py第154行，知识检索功能完全不可用

signals.topic: Multi-agent MsgHub causes agent memory to leak other agents' thinking content
signals.summary: When multiple agents chat via MsgHub, an agent's memory sometimes includes other agents' thinking processes, polluting its context and causing confusing behavior. Not always reproducible, making it a subtle but impactful bug.
aliases: agent memory contains other agents thinking
智能体记忆包含其他智能体思考过程
signals.review_reason: 多智能体协作是agentscope的核心场景，agent记忆被其他agent的thinking污染会导致：上下文混乱、回复质量下降、对话逻辑错误。虽然非100%必现，但属于严重的会话状态泄露，直接破坏多智能体架构的隔离性。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: 多智能体在msghub 聊天 ，智能体记忆会包含其他智能体的思考过程
source_issues.evidence: 多智能体通过MsgHub共享消息时，某个agent的记忆中包含其他agent的thinking内容（通过截图证据可见），导致agent上下文被污染，回复混乱。这是多智能体协作的核心功能缺陷，影响所有使用MsgHub的用户

signals.topic: Qwen3 model with vllm reasoning parser misconfiguration causes thinking content parsing failure
signals.summary: When using Qwen3 model with vllm and reasoning-parser=deepseek_r1 (instead of qwen3), non-streaming output with thinking enabled/disabled causes parsing errors and empty thinking content. The wrong parser config leads to reasoning content in wrong field.
signals.review_reason: 用户配置错误parser时agentscope未能给出明确提示，导致thinking内容完全为空。这是reasoning解析支持不完善的问题，影响使用Qwen3+vllm的用户。但count=1且为配置相关，非框架阻断性bug。

source_issues.title: [Bug]:qwen3 vllm非流式输出下解析bug
source_issues.evidence: Qwen3模型+vllm+reasoning-parser=deepseek_r1时，非流式输出配合思考开关会导致解析异常，thinking内容跑到错误字段导致显示为空。用户被迫使用正确的reasoning-parser=qwen3，但agentscope没有对此进行正确引导或报错

signals.topic: Anthropic Provider strips server_tool_use and code execution tool result blocks from message history, causing Claude to re-run code indefinitely
signals.summary: agno format_messages() discards server_tool_use, bash_code_execution_tool_result, and text_editor_code_execution_tool_result blocks. Without these in history, Claude loses memory of code it executed and believes files were never created, triggering infinite loops of code execution and get_generated_file calls.
aliases: Anthropic code execution blocks stripped from history
file skills not properly handling file ids and container reuse
signals.review_reason: Claude code execution within agno enters an infinite loop — Claude repeatedly calls tools believing files were never created. This causes unbounded token waste and blocks the user's intended workflow entirely. Two independent reports covering related aspects of the same root cause.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Anthropic Provider block/removes key tool events for code execution and files
source_issues.evidence: format_messages() silently removes server_tool_use and *_code_execution_tool_result blocks; Claude enters infinite loop calling get_generated_file and re-running code; Agno 2.5.10/11 confirmed affected

source_issues.title: [Bug] not properly handling files and container in claude model
source_issues.evidence: File ids are not captured and container ids are not reused across Claude file skill interactions; prevents users from continuing to manipulate files created by Claude

signals.topic: VertexAI/Bedrock Claude API calls completely blocked by TypeError after upgrading to v2.5.11
signals.summary: In v2.5.11, AnthropicClaude._prepare_request_kwargs added a 'messages' parameter, but the VertexAI and AWS Bedrock child class overrides were not updated, causing TypeError on every API call for all VertexAI and Bedrock Claude users.
aliases: Bedrock Claude parameter mismatch after upgrade
signals.review_reason: Every API call for all VertexAI and Bedrock Claude users is blocked by a TypeError immediately after upgrading to 2.5.11. This is a hard failure that makes the integration completely unusable, with clear reproduction steps and explicit root cause. Marked P1 (not P0) because count=1.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Critical: VertexAI and Bedrock Claude: `_prepare_request_kwargs() got unexpected keyword argument 'messages'` after 2.5.11
source_issues.evidence: TypeError on every API call; both affected classes (vertexai/claude.py line 156, aws/claude.py line 225) fail with the same error immediately after upgrade to 2.5.11; users must monkey-patch the child class to work around

signals.topic: Workflow Step crashes with NoneType AttributeError when Team executor fails silently
signals.summary: When a Team executor encounters an internal error and yields TeamRunErrorEvent instead of TeamRunOutput, the Step's aexecute_stream passes None to _store_executor_response, causing AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'parent_run_id'. The Step retries 4 times and then the entire Workflow fails.
aliases: Workflow Team executor error crashes step
signals.review_reason: Workflow execution is blocked when using Team as a step with stream=True; the crash is unrecoverable (4 retries all fail), and the underlying Team error is masked, making debugging impossible. Confirmed bug with clear reproduction path.

source_issues.title: [Bug] AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'parent_run_id' in Workflow Step when Team executor doesn't yield RunOutput
source_issues.evidence: Step crashes unconditionally when Team executor returns None (4 retries × instant failure); the real Team error is completely hidden behind the secondary AttributeError; reproduction with Team + Workflow + stream=True confirmed; related issues #5451 and #5379 reference the same pattern

signals.topic: enable_agentic_state=True fails silently — session state never updated despite confirmation
signals.summary: When enable_agentic_state=True is set, the agent textual replies confirm triggering update_session_state but the actual session_state in the database remains unchanged (empty dict). Users following the official agentic-session-state example end up with no persisted state.
aliases: enable_agentic_state parameter not propagated to state management tool
signals.review_reason: Core advertised feature (agentic session state) is broken despite using the official example. The state is silently lost — no error thrown but data is not persisted, making the feature unusable. Clear user impact on a documented feature.

source_issues.title: [Bug] enable_agentic_state is not working even with example agentic-session-state
source_issues.evidence: Official example code produces empty session state; agent claims to have triggered update_session_state but state remains {}; traced to parameter not being correctly passed to the state-management tool; GPT-5-mini confirmed

signals.topic: Team delegate_task_to_member returns raw streaming tokens instead of structured output when stream=True
signals.summary: When a parent Team delegates to a member agent with stream=True, the delegate_task_to_member tool result contains all concatenated RunContentEvent tokens from the member's streaming response instead of the clean final output. stream=False correctly returns JSON.
aliases: Team streaming delegate returns concatenated raw tokens
signals.review_reason: Team streaming with delegation produces corrupted output that breaks the parent Team's ability to process member results. The answer is present but buried in a blob of raw tokens, making it functionally unusable for streaming Team workflows.

source_issues.title: [Bug] `delegate_task_to_member` tool result contains raw streaming tokens instead of final output when `stream=True`
source_issues.evidence: 3-level Team hierarchy (Coordinator→Verifier→Research Agent) confirmed; stream=False returns clean JSON, stream=True returns massive concatenated blob; actual answer buried at end of blob; step-by-step reproduction provided

signals.topic: TUI: session sidebar overlaps content on narrow terminals instead of docking cleanly
signals.summary: On narrower laptop-sized terminals in the TUI, the right-hand session sidebar behaves like an overlay instead of a docked panel, covering chat content and the input area instead of resizing the main content column.
aliases: TUI sidebar overlay on narrow screens
session sidebar not resizing properly on small terminals
signals.review_reason: TUI sidebar overlay is a UX-blocking issue on narrow laptop screens — a common real-world terminal size. The main chat content and input area become inaccessible or unreadable. Two separate reporters (including one with before/after screenshots) filed this in the same hour, indicating it is not an isolated edge case.

source_issues.title: TUI: session sidebar overlaps content instead of docking cleanly on narrow terminals
source_issues.evidence: Sidebar overlays chat content and input area on narrow terminals. Conversation column does not shrink when sidebar is visible. Reporter confirmed with before/after screenshots. Issue was closed as duplicate of #19450.

source_issues.title: TUI: session sidebar overlaps content instead of docking cleanly on narrow terminals
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate of #19448. Sidebar may not auto-dock when there's enough room, and when visible covers the active session instead of staying alongside the main column.

signals.topic: Snapshot path migration in v1.3.3 causes Review tab to show empty diffs for pre-upgrade sessions
signals.summary: After upgrading to v1.3.3, the Review tab shows no diffs for sessions created before the upgrade. The snapshot gitdir path was restructured but existing objects were not migrated, causing the `from` hash to reference a non-existent tree object.
signals.review_reason: v1.3.3 upgrade silently breaks the Review tab for all pre-existing sessions — a critical feature becomes completely non-functional. The issue has detailed reproduction steps, root cause analysis confirmed by the reporter, and a manual workaround. Users lose access to session diff review without any warning during upgrade.

source_issues.title: Snapshot path migration in v1.3.3 breaks Review tab for pre-existing sessions
source_issues.evidence: Review tab shows empty diffs for all pre-upgrade sessions. session_diff/<session-id>.json contains [], summary_files=0, summary_additions=0, summary_deletions=0. Both Session and Last Turn views are affected. User has to manually copy objects between repos as workaround.

signals.topic: Client state clobbered when running multiple OpenCode instances simultaneously
signals.summary: When two or more OpenCode instances are open, client state files (kv.json, prompt-history.jsonl, etc.) are race-condition clobbered, causing user preferences like theme changes to be silently lost.
signals.review_reason: Running multiple OpenCode instances is a normal, expected usage pattern. The race condition in state file writes silently discards user preferences without any warning. Theme changes and sidebar state are lost permanently after closing and reopening. This directly degrades the user experience and erodes trust in the application's state management.

source_issues.title: client state clobbered w/ multiple instances of opencode
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible: open two instances, change theme in instance 1, show sidebar in instance 2, close both and reopen — theme change is gone. Affects kv.json, prompt-history.jsonl, frecency.jsonl, models.json.

signals.topic: OpenCode Desktop: clicking VS Code button opens wrong window instead of the project directory
signals.summary: On Windows 11, clicking the VS Code button in OpenCode Desktop opens VS Code with two empty files instead of the project folder, breaking the intended IDE integration workflow.
aliases: VS Code integration broken on Windows Desktop
OpenCode Desktop fails to open VS Code in correct directory on Windows
signals.review_reason: OpenCode Desktop's VS Code integration is a core workflow feature on Windows. The button fails to open the correct project directory, forcing users to manually navigate to the project in VS Code. This is a key IDE integration feature being non-functional on the desktop app for Windows users.

source_issues.title: Clicking on VS Code doesn't work - OpenCode Desktop Windows 11
source_issues.evidence: Clicking VS Code button opens two empty files in VS Code instead of the project folder. Reproduced on Windows 11, OpenCode Desktop 1.3.3. Screenshots provided showing empty VS Code window.

signals.topic: TUI: chat history cannot be scrolled up; text ordering breaks after window resize with extra punctuation appearing
signals.summary: In the OpenCode CLI TUI, the scroll wheel/trackpad cannot scroll up through chat history. Window resize temporarily restores scrolling but causes text misalignment and random punctuation characters appear during typing.
aliases: TUI scroll stuck in chat history
chat history text scrambling on window resize
signals.review_reason: Chat history scrolling is a fundamental TUI interaction. Inability to review previous messages blocks the user's ability to reference past context, which is a core use case. Text scrambling and random punctuation further degrade the experience. While the issue is from a single reporter, the symptoms are severe and reproducible.

source_issues.title: Chat history scroll issue - cannot scroll up, text order gets scrambled after window resize/movement
source_issues.evidence: Cannot scroll up through chat history using scroll wheel or trackpad. Window resize is required as a workaround but causes text misalignment. Random punctuation appears while typing. Screenshots provided. Reproduced on Windows 10.

signals.topic: Tests fail on i386 (32-bit) architecture due to int overflow
signals.summary: 用户在 32 位架构（i386）上打包或运行测试时，测试代码中的大整数字面量（237628372683）超出 int 范围导致编译失败，阻断测试流程
signals.review_reason: 虽然仅 1 条 issue，但属于主流程阻断：32 位系统上测试完全无法编译通过，Debian 包维护者无法完成打包验证。这不是纯功能请求或路线图讨论，而是已在生产环境中实际触发的阻断问题，影响所有在 i386 架构上使用该 SDK 的用户。

source_issues.title: Tests fail on i386 (32 bit)
source_issues.evidence: 测试编译错误：多个 apiform/apijson/apiquery 测试文件中使用 untyped int constant 237628372683 在 i386 (32-bit) 编译时报 overflow，导致 Debian i386 打包测试失败。错误涉及 form_test.go、json_test.go、query_test.go 共 12+ 处编译失败。

signals.topic: Mid-stream SSE errors report status_code=200 instead of actual error code
signals.summary: SSE 流式响应中途出现 API 错误（如 overloaded_error）时，SDK 错误码报为 200 而非真实错误码（如 529），导致依赖 status_code 的重试/降级逻辑完全失效。
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：OverloadedError 应触发 fallback/retry 逻辑但 status_code 报为 200，导致生产环境的重试系统完全失效。pydantic-ai 等主流框架依赖 status_code 做降级判断，此 bug 使其永不触发。

source_issues.title: Mid-stream SSE errors get status_code=200 instead of the actual error code
source_issues.evidence: When the API returns HTTP 200 (streaming started fine) but then sends an SSE error event like overloaded_error, the SDK creates APIStatusError with status_code=200 instead of 529. Caller checking status_code for retry/fallback decisions gets wrong answer. pydantic-ai's FallbackModel checks status_code >= 500 to decide whether to try next model - fallback never fires because overloaded error had status_code=200.

signals.topic: MCP connectors non-functional — Etherscan MCP egress proxy blocked at network level
signals.summary: $200/月 Pro 订阅用户无法使用 claude.ai 上宣传的 MCP 集成，Etherscan MCP 连接器在出口代理层被 HTTP 403 屏蔽。
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用：$200/月 Pro 订阅用户无法使用官方宣传的 MCP 集成。产品设计层面失败——egress 代理未放行已列出 MCP 服务商的域名。

source_issues.title: MCP connectors non-functional on claude.ai — mcp.etherscan.io hardblocked at network level
source_issues.evidence: Pro subscribers paying $200/month cannot use advertised MCP integrations. Etherscan MCP connector is hardblocked at egress proxy level (HTTP 403 with x-deny-reason: host_not_allowed). Both mcp.etherscan.io and api.etherscan.io are blocked.

signals.topic: web_search_20250209 dynamic filtering causes excessive pause_turn (50-60% failure rate)
signals.summary: web_search_20250209 工具在 Messages API 中动态过滤阶段频繁进入 code_execution 内部循环，50-60% 请求返回 pause_turn 导致批处理任务无法完成，已在多个生态框架引发关联 issue。
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：生产批次任务 50-60% 失败率使工具完全不可用于自动化流程。同时导致成本损失——失败请求仍全额计费。已在 Pydantic AI、LiteLLM、LangChain、Vercel AI SDK 等生态多处引发关联 issue。

source_issues.title: web_search_20250209 dynamic filtering causes excessive pause_turn at ~110 content blocks — batch processing impractical
source_issues.evidence: When using web_search_20250209 with Messages API, model frequently enters internal loop of code_execution calls during dynamic filtering. 50-60% of requests return stop_reason='pause_turn' with ~110 content blocks — no usable output. Batch of 35 requests takes 9+ hours and typically completes only 50-60% of items. Failed attempts still incur full token costs. Causing issues across ecosystem: Pydantic AI #2600, LiteLLM #17737, LangChain #33920, Vercel AI SDK #11855.

signals.topic: Gift subscription redeemed but account stuck on Free plan with no working support channel
signals.summary: 用户兑换 Claude Max 礼品订阅后账户仍显示 Free 计划，支持门户页面空白无法提交工单，邮件支持仅能联系 AI bot 无法转人工，连续 7 天以上付费权益损失。
signals.review_reason: 付费用户主流程失败：礼品订阅未生效，同时支持渠道完全失效（Portal 空白页、AI bot 无法转人工），连续 7 天以上付费权益损失且无解决路径。产品失败与客服失败双重叠加。

source_issues.title: Gift subscription redeemed but account stuck on Free plan – no human support available
source_issues.evidence: User redeemed Claude Max gift subscription over a week ago. Redemption page confirms 'This gift has already been redeemed' but account still shows Free plan. Support portal shows blank page after login — cannot submit ticket. Email support only connects to AI bot which cannot perform backend operations or connect to human agents. 7+ days of paid Max plan access lost with no resolution path available.

signals.topic: beta.skills.create intermittently fails with Cloudflare 520/502 errors
signals.summary: SDK 调用 client.beta.skills.create() 稳定复现 Cloudflare 520/502 错误，而同环境下 curl 和 SDK 的 list() 均成功，问题指向 SDK 请求构造/序列化缺陷。
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：SDK 稳定复现失败而 curl 同环境成功，问题指向 SDK 请求构造/序列化缺陷，用户无法通过 SDK 创建 skills。

source_issues.title: beta.skills.create intermittently fails with Cloudflare 520/502 (anthropic SDK python 0.86.0)
source_issues.evidence: When using the Anthropic Python SDK, client.beta.skills.create(...) consistently fails with Cloudflare errors (520 Web server is returning an unknown error / 502 Bad Gateway). In the same environment, client.beta.skills.list(...) succeeds. curl succeeds while SDK fails, suggesting SDK request construction/serialization issue.

signals.topic: Streaming connection termination with large inputs in undici-based SDK
signals.summary: Users encounter TypeError: terminated errors when streaming large inputs (large files, long tool call sequences) with the undici-based SDK (v0.71.2+), causing streaming requests to crash unexpectedly.
signals.review_reason: Streaming is a primary workflow path for the SDK. The TypeError: terminated is a main-flow crash with no graceful error handling — it directly blocks users processing large documents. The issue is reproducible, affects multiple model versions (Sonnet 4.5, 4.6, Haiku 4.5), and provides no workaround path. This is a high-severity runtime failure.

source_issues.title: TypeError: terminated during streaming requests with large inputs (Anthropic SDK 0.71.2 / undici)
source_issues.evidence: TypeError: terminated thrown from undici Fetch.onAborted during streaming of large file processing with multi-tool calls. Crash is reproducible when prompts involve large source analysis or file creation >1500 lines. No retry guidance or deterministic error — abrupt failure.

signals.topic: Claude 4.6 models regress to single tool call in Message Batches API, breaking parallel extraction pipelines
signals.summary: Claude Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 models only produce 1 tool call in the Message Batches API regardless of tool_choice settings or available output tokens, while Opus 4.5 correctly produces 39+ parallel tool calls — a production-blocking regression for multi-tool extraction workflows.
aliases: 4.6 batch API single tool call regression
batch API tool call count regression 4.6
signals.review_reason: While count=1, the user provides a thorough test matrix with reproducible results across multiple 4.6 model variants, explicit token budgets, and system prompt variations. This is a production-blocking regression: medical extraction pipelines produce incomplete data (1 of 46 fields). The regression is clearly attributed to model version (4.5→4.6) rather than SDK config. P1 is appropriate given single-issue evidence; P0 reserved for count≥3 cases.

source_issues.title: Claude Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 fail to make parallel tool calls in Batch API
source_issues.evidence: Production medical document pipeline broken: with 46 extraction tools and 64K+ output tokens, Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 call exactly 1 tool and stop (stop_reason: 'tool_use'). Same request with Opus 4.5 correctly calls 39+ tools. Workaround exists (downgrade to Opus 4.5) but blocks access to 4.6 intelligence and 128K output capacity.

signals.topic: Missing TypeScript types for Tool Search functionality in vertex-sdk
signals.summary: The @anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk package lacks TypeScript type definitions for Tool Search tools (tool_search_tool_regex_20251119, tool_search_tool_bm25_20251119) and the defer_loading property, forcing developers to use unsafe 'as any' workarounds.
signals.review_reason: Missing type definitions cause TypeScript compilation failures and force unsafe 'as any' workarounds. This directly degrades developer experience and removes compile-time safety guarantees for a documented API feature. The runtime API works, confirming the types are simply absent from the SDK.

source_issues.title: [Feature]: Missing TypeScript types for Tool Search functionality
source_issues.evidence: TypeScript compilation fails when using tool_search_tool_regex_20251119 and defer_loading. Developers forced to cast with 'as any' — a type-safety violation that masks potential runtime errors. API supports these features at runtime; SDK types are simply missing.

signals.topic: O(N²) performance bottleneck in MessageStream during structured output streaming
signals.summary: MessageStream re-parses the entire cumulative JSON buffer on every streaming delta, causing O(N²) complexity that leads to high CPU usage and UI freezing on long structured output responses.
signals.review_reason: Performance degradation causing UI freezing is a significant user-experience impact. O(N²) behavior means it becomes progressively worse with response length, directly affecting real-world streaming use cases. Proposed fix (lazy getter) is well-scoped.

source_issues.title: O(N²) performance bottleneck in MessageStream during structured output streaming
source_issues.evidence: MessageStream eagerly calls partialParse(jsonBuf) on every delta, re-parsing the full cumulative buffer each time. For long responses this causes high CPU usage and UI freezing — a clear performance regression for structured output workflows.

signals.topic: toBase64 utility crashes with stack overflow on large inputs in browser and non-Node environments
signals.summary: The toBase64 utility crashes with 'Maximum call stack size exceeded' when processing inputs larger than ~100KB in standard browsers, Cloudflare Workers, and other non-Node environments due to lack of native Buffer support.
signals.review_reason: Stack overflow is a runtime crash that blocks image upload workflows in browser and edge environments. Image uploads of typical sizes (>100KB) will crash, which is a common SDK use case. The crash is deterministic and reproducible.

source_issues.title: toBase64 stack overflow on large inputs (e.g. image uploads) in non-Node environments
source_issues.evidence: RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded when calling toBase64 with Uint8Array > ~100KB in browser or Cloudflare Workers. Image upload use cases with typical image sizes are directly affected. Non-Node environments lack Buffer, exposing this crash path.

signals.topic: Skills called via SDK query() fail to retrieve data, while direct skill calls succeed
signals.summary: When using the `query()` API to invoke a skill, the skill fails to return data, but calling the same skill directly works. Both paths use the same model. This indicates the SDK's skill invocation path has a functional regression that prevents data retrieval through the agent abstraction.
aliases: skill invocation via SDK returns empty data
SDK skill call no data returned
signals.review_reason: This is a user-reported functional failure where the SDK's primary skill invocation path (query() with Skill tool) silently fails to return data, while direct skill calls succeed. The user explicitly identifies this as a regression affecting the main workflow of using skills through the agent SDK. The 'workflow_runtime' category applies as the skill execution path is broken. Confidence is capped at 0.75 because only one issue report is available, but the evidence is specific and reproducible by the user.

source_issues.title: agent-sdk use skills fail, but I can directly use the skill to return the data.
source_issues.evidence: User reports that calling a skill via `query()` returns no data, while calling the same skill directly (same model) successfully returns data. This is a functional regression that blocks the primary SDK usage pattern for skill-based workflows.

signals.topic: Sub-agents fail to load; model falls back to general-purpose agent instead of specified role
signals.summary: Defined sub-agents (e.g., researcher, data analyst) cannot be loaded correctly. When executing tasks, the model calls the general-purpose agent instead of the intended specialized sub-agent, breaking the multi-agent architecture pattern.
aliases: sub-agent not loaded fallback to general-purpose agent
signals.review_reason: Sub-agent loading is a core architectural feature of the SDK demos. When sub-agents fail to load and the model silently falls back to a general-purpose agent, users lose the multi-agent specialization pattern this SDK is designed to demonstrate. This blocks the intended workflow for research-agent and similar multi-agent demos. The 2-comment thread indicates this is a non-trivial issue with community impact.

source_issues.title: research-agent subagent problem
source_issues.evidence: User reports that defined sub-agents cannot be loaded; the model substitutes a general-purpose agent instead of the researcher or data analyst role. This has 2 comments indicating ongoing discussion and impact on the research-agent demo workflow.

signals.topic: SDK MCP tool calls fail with 'Stream closed' after ~70s due to bundled CLI inactivity timer not resetting on MCP responses
signals.summary: When using custom MCP tools via create_sdk_mcp_server, all MCP tool calls fail with 'Stream closed' after ~60-70 seconds of operation. Built-in tools (Read, Grep) continue working. Root cause: the bundled Claude CLI does not reset lastActivityTime when MCP server responses arrive, causing the inactivity timer to exceed the stream close threshold.
signals.review_reason: Custom MCP tools become completely non-functional after ~70s during active sessions. Tool calls are immediately rejected with 'Stream closed' (1-5ms response time proves tool never ran). This is a main-flow failure for any long-running MCP workflow (log analysis, git operations, etc.). Evidence from JSONL session logs provides concrete timestamps ruling out timeout variation. TypeScript SDK has a confirmed fix (resetLastActivityTime), confirming root cause.

source_issues.title: [BUG] SDK MCP server tool calls fail with 'Stream closed' after ~70s - Python SDK v0.1.47
source_issues.evidence: JSONL session logs show tool_call and tool_result 'Stream closed' (is_error=true) timestamps differ by only 1-5ms, proving the tool never executed. Built-in tools in the same session succeed normally. Root cause identified as bundled CLI not calling resetLastActivityTime() on MCP responses, same as TS SDK issue #114 with verified fix.

signals.topic: query() with hooks closes stdin after 60s hardcoded timeout, killing active hook callbacks mid-conversation
signals.summary: When using query() with SDK hooks (PreToolUse/PostToolUse), the SDK closes stdin after a 60-second timeout via wait_for_result_and_end_input(), even if the CLI is still actively processing and sending hook callback requests. This kills the bidirectional control protocol and causes 'Tool permission stream closed before response received' errors.
signals.review_reason: Any query() session with hooks running longer than 60s has all subsequent hook callbacks fail catastrophically. This breaks the core bidirectional control protocol between SDK and CLI. The failure cascades to an unhandled TaskGroup exception. Direct user impact is observable and reproducible via the provided MRE. While a workaround exists, requiring manual env var configuration for every long-running hook session is a significant UX degradation.

source_issues.title: query() with hooks closes stdin after 60s timeout, killing hook callbacks mid-conversation
source_issues.evidence: MRE provided shows SDK closes stdin via wait_for_result_and_end_input() with 60s default (CLAUDE_CODE_STREAM_CLOSE_TIMEOUT). After stdin closes, CLI stderr shows 'Error in hook callback hook_0: ... Tool permission stream closed before response received'. This propagates as 'unhandled errors in a TaskGroup (1 sub-exception)'. Workaround exists (set CLAUDE_CODE_STREAM_CLOSE_TIMEOUT=3600000) but requires manual configuration.

signals.topic: SubprocessCLITransport.close() hangs indefinitely when Claude Code subprocess shutdown handler blocks
signals.summary: SubprocessCLITransport.close() sends SIGTERM to the Claude Code subprocess, then calls await self._process.wait() with no timeout. If the Node.js process runs a shutdown handler that blocks (e.g., waiting for MCP server or subagent exit), process.wait() blocks forever. Caused 30% of parallel jobs to hang in production.
aliases: VM infra timeout due to SDK hang
signals.review_reason: Indefinite hang in close() is a process lifecycle bug that causes cascading infrastructure failures (worker processes hitting VM timeouts). 30% reproduction rate in parallel workload (~60 out of 200 jobs) is a severe, observable impact. The hang is deterministic when the subprocess shutdown handler blocks, not a race condition. Suggested fix (wrap in anyio.fail_after with configurable timeout) is straightforward.

source_issues.title: SubprocessCLITransport.close() hangs indefinitely if subprocess shutdown handler blocks
source_issues.evidence: User reports that in their use case running ~200 parallel Claude Code instances via SDK, 30% of jobs hung indefinitely. Claude Code job finished successfully but VM stayed hanging because SDK's transport.close() never returned, causing the entire worker process to hit VM infra timeout. 30% reproduction rate provides statistical weight to a single report.

signals.topic: Long-running subagent output includes SendMessage hint but tool does not exist, causing parent agent failure loop and lost work
signals.summary: When a subagent completes (or is cut off by token/turn limits), its final output includes 'agentId: ... (use SendMessage ...)' hint. The parent agent attempts to call SendMessage tool, which does not exist in the SDK toolset, resulting in 'No such tool available: SendMessage' error. Parent agent enters a failure loop and subagent's work is lost.
aliases: agentId hint causes tool call failure
signals.review_reason: Subagent work is silently lost when session ends naturally (token/turn limits), with no recovery mechanism. Parent agent enters a failure loop attempting to call a non-existent tool, blocking further conversation progress. The 'workaround' (complete all work before session ends) is not a solution — it's a constraint that defeats the purpose of multi-agent architecture. This is a main workflow blocker for any multi-agent pipeline.

source_issues.title: Bug: Long-running subagent returns agentId with SendMessage hint, but SendMessage tool does not exist
source_issues.evidence: Error message captured: '<tool_use_error>Error: No such tool available: SendMessage</tool_use_error>'. The 'agentId: ... use SendMessage ...' footer is emitted by Claude Code CLI internally. Parent agent treats it as a real tool instruction and enters failure loop. Zero references to SendMessage in repo source code. Workaround described: subagent must complete all work before session ends — meaning results are silently lost if interrupted.

signals.topic: InternalClient.process_query() does not pass initialize_timeout to Query(), ignoring CLAUDE_CODE_STREAM_CLOSE_TIMEOUT env var
signals.summary: The query() function path uses InternalClient.process_query() which creates a Query() without passing initialize_timeout. This means CLAUDE_CODE_STREAM_CLOSE_TIMEOUT has no effect on the initialize handshake timeout for query() users — it's always hardcoded 60s. ClaudeSDKClient.connect() correctly reads the env var but the query() path does not.
signals.review_reason: Users relying on query() (vs ClaudeSDKClient) with slow MCP servers or large project directories cannot configure the initialize timeout, hitting hardcoded 60s limit. Direct code comparison proves the inconsistency between two SDK code paths handling the same env var differently. The bug makes the query() path strictly less capable than ClaudeSDKClient for timeout-sensitive use cases.

source_issues.title: InternalClient.process_query() does not pass initialize_timeout to Query, causing 60s hardcoded timeout
source_issues.evidence: Code comparison shows ClaudeSDKClient.connect() (client.py lines 149-173) correctly reads env var and passes initialize_timeout, while InternalClient.process_query() (_internal/client.py) does not pass the parameter at all. Reproduction code shows query() times out at ~60s regardless of CLAUDE_CODE_STREAM_CLOSE_TIMEOUT setting. Impact stated: 'Any user of query() with slow MCP servers or large project directories will hit the 60s timeout regardless of configuration.'

signals.topic: Empty settingSources array blocks all default query() calls — CLI flag consumption error
signals.summary: When settingSources is not explicitly provided to query(), the SDK passes --setting-sources "" to the CLI, which consumes the next flag (--permission-mode) as its value, causing 'Invalid setting source: --permission-mode' on every default SDK usage. The client() constructor has the same issue. This is a complete workflow blocker for all new users and any default query() invocation.
aliases: settingSources empty array CLI flag consumption
signals.review_reason: This is a primary workflow blocker: every single default query() invocation fails immediately due to empty string argument consumption. New users cannot use the SDK out of the box. The reproduction case is a one-liner 'for await (const msg of query("Say hello"))' which completely breaks. No user can work around this without knowing to set settingSources explicitly, and the workaround requires non-obvious domain knowledge.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Empty settingSources array causes --setting-sources "" to consume next CLI flag
source_issues.evidence: Any query() call without explicit settingSources fails with 'Error processing --setting-sources: Invalid setting source: --permission-mode'. Reproducible with the simplest possible SDK call. The client() constructor has the same hardcoded empty array issue.

signals.topic: output_tokens sum from assistant messages does not match result message — cost tracking broken
signals.summary: When iterating over query() messages with includePartialMessages: false (the default), summing message.usage.output_tokens from all assistant messages yields a value that does not equal the output_tokens in the final result message. This breaks all cost tracking and usage accounting workflows built on top of the SDK, causing billing discrepancies and silent overcharging.
signals.review_reason: Cost tracking is a core integration use case for SDK users building production pipelines. A systematic output_tokens mismatch means every application relying on the documented cost tracking pattern reports incorrect billing data. This is not a rare edge case — it affects the default SDK configuration on every query. While only one issue is filed, the root cause is a systematic bug in the token accumulation logic, not a configuration issue.

source_issues.title: [BUG] sum of output_tokens from "assistant" messages returned by query() doesn't equal output_tokens of the "result" message
source_issues.evidence: The user's computed output_tokens sum (78) diverges from the result message's output_tokens (275) — a -197 difference. The issue is reproducible with the default includePartialMessages: false setting. Input, cache creation, and cache read tokens all sum correctly; only output_tokens is wrong. This directly causes billing discrepancies for any user monitoring costs programmatically.

signals.topic: dangerouslyDisableSandbox executes without user approval after prior tool call rejection
signals.summary: After a user explicitly rejects a tool call that would require sandbox disable, and then retries (with auto-allow or same session), the dangerouslyDisableSandbox command executes without prompting for user permission. This is a security boundary bypass where the user's rejection is silently overridden.
signals.review_reason: This is a security-critical issue: a sandbox boundary that users explicitly opted out of is silently bypassed. The user rejection is overridden by the retry path, causing arbitrary code execution outside the sandbox without consent. This directly violates the security model of dangerouslyDisableSandbox and can lead to data exposure or system compromise. The behavior is reproducible and blocks the safety guarantee that sandbox rejections should provide.

source_issues.title: [BUG] dangerouslyDisableSandbox executed without user approval after prior rejection
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly rejected a tool call requesting sandbox disable, then rejected and retried. The tool executed without permission. Logs show the sequence: tool call → user rejects → retry attempt → execution without approval prompt. The dangerous shell command ran outside the sandbox without any permission UI being shown.

signals.topic: Prompt caching fails with MCP servers — cache invalidates on every resume query()
signals.summary: When MCP servers are configured, prompt caching fails to work across resume query() calls. The cache is invalidated on every resume, forcing full cache regeneration. This invalidates the primary cost optimization use case for MCP-enabled SDK deployments and causes significant unnecessary API costs.
signals.review_reason: Prompt caching is a major cost optimization feature (up to 98% input cost reduction). MCP servers are a first-class SDK feature. When combining the two breaks caching on every multi-turn session, users lose the primary cost benefit of the SDK. This is not a cosmetic issue — it causes real monetary loss on every query in MCP-enabled deployments. Users are forced to choose between MCP tools and caching efficiency, a forced tradeoff that should not exist.

source_issues.title: Prompt Caching is failing with MCP Servers
source_issues.evidence: User restructured application to use HTTP-based MCP after discovering SDK MCP server was not serializable. Even with HTTP MCP, caching still fails on resume queries. Removing MCP servers from setup restores caching. The non-serializable SdkMcpServer also prevents session storage, compounding the cache loss on every resume.

signals.topic: ExitWorktree fails with 'no active session' when worktree was created in an earlier query() call
signals.summary: When a worktree is created via EnterWorktree in one query() invocation, a subsequent query() with the same session ID cannot exit the worktree — ExitWorktree returns 'no active EnterWorktree session'. Worktree session state is not persisted across separate query() calls, breaking multi-turn session patterns that rely on session ID continuity.
aliases: Worktree state not persisted across query calls
signals.review_reason: EnterWorktree/ExitWorktree is a key session management feature. When the session state is lost between query() calls with the same session ID, users cannot implement legitimate multi-turn workflows that involve worktrees — a core documented use case. This breaks the session continuity promise of the SDK, leaving orphaned worktrees on disk and preventing proper cleanup. The worktree persists but the SDK forgets about it, creating an inconsistent state.

source_issues.title: ExitWorktree claims "no active EnterWorktree session" if worktree created in earlier query()
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction shows EnterWorktree creates a worktree successfully in query() call 1, but ExitWorktree with the same session ID in query() call 2 returns 'no active EnterWorktree session to exit'. The worktree persists on disk but the SDK loses the in-memory session state. A minimal reproducible repo is available.

signals.topic: GitHub token lacks pull-requests:write permission — action silently exits 0 with no review output
signals.summary: When the GitHub token used by the action lacks `pull-requests: write` permission, the action receives a 403 from the GitHub API but exits 0 (success), producing no review output anywhere. Users have no feedback loop to detect the misconfiguration.
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow blocker: the entire purpose of the action (posting a code review) fails silently with no error signal. The workflow reports green while producing zero output. Users cannot distinguish a successful run from a permission-misconfigured run. Evidence is specific: 403 from GitHub API is caught and swallowed, exit code is 0.

source_issues.title: claude-code-review workflow template generates insufficient permissions; action silently swallows write failure
source_issues.evidence: Action attempts to post review comment, receives 403 from GitHub API due to insufficient permissions, but exits 0. Job reports success with no indication that the review was never written. No feedback loop — template is wrong, action doesn't complain, job shows green, reviews silently go nowhere.

signals.topic: Sticky comment feature silently fails in agent mode — MCP server starts without CLAUDE_COMMENT_ID, comment never created
signals.summary: When use_sticky_comment is true but the action enters agent mode (track_progress: false with a prompt), the sticky comment is silently ignored. The MCP server starts without CLAUDE_COMMENT_ID in its environment, every update call fails, and no comment ever appears on the PR.
signals.review_reason: A key feature (sticky comments) fails silently with zero user-facing indication of failure. The action reports success while the primary output (the comment on the PR) is never created. This is a complete feature failure, not a degradation. Specific root cause identified: hardcoded undefined claudeCommentId in agent/index.ts line 105.

source_issues.title: `use_sticky_comment` has no effect in agent mode — MCP server starts without CLAUDE_COMMENT_ID
source_issues.evidence: In agent mode, claudeCommentId is hardcoded to undefined. shouldIncludeCommentServer evaluates to true but MCP server starts without CLAUDE_COMMENT_ID. Every update_claude_comment call fails with 'CLAUDE_COMMENT_ID environment variable is required'. Action completes successfully but no sticky comment ever appears on the PR.

signals.topic: claude-code-action crashes on self-hosted runners without AVX CPU support
signals.summary: The action is built with Bun, which requires AVX CPU instructions. On self-hosted runners with older CPUs lacking AVX support, the action crashes immediately with 'Illegal instruction' during bun run, blocking all Claude Code execution.
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow blocker for self-hosted runner users on non-AVX hardware. The action crashes immediately before any Claude work begins, with 'Illegal instruction' from bun. User's entire CI/CD pipeline is blocked. Evidence confirms the npm version works on the same hardware, proving the issue is the Bun-based packaging, not the hardware itself.

source_issues.title: Action fails on runners without AVX CPU support
source_issues.evidence: Action crashes immediately with 'Illegal instruction' when bun run is executed on self-hosted runner without AVX support. The crash occurs at 'bun run ${GITHUB_ACTION_PATH}/src/entrypoints/post-buffered-inline-comments.ts'. The npm version of claude works fine on non-AVX hardware. User is blocked from using the action on their self-hosted infrastructure.

signals.topic: Using anthropic_api_key with Claude Code subscription returns misleading 'Credit balance is too low' error
signals.summary: Setting up the action with a valid anthropic_api_key (with credits on platform.claude.com) fails with 'Credit balance is too low'. The real issue is that the action requires a Claude Code subscription or OAuth token, not just API credits, but this is not communicated to users.
signals.review_reason: This blocks the initial setup of the action — the most critical first-time user experience. The error message ('Credit balance is too low') is actively misleading, directing users to add credits when they actually need a different credential type entirely. README documentation implies anthropic_api_key is sufficient when it is not for this use case. Users waste time and money on the wrong solution.

source_issues.title: anthropic_api_key insufficient - misleading 'Credit balance is too low' error when Claude Code subscription required
source_issues.evidence: User sets up action with valid anthropic_api_key (fresh key, $30 USD balance on platform.claude.com). Action fails instantly with 'Credit balance is too low' (duration_ms: 180, total_cost_usd: 0). No indication that the credential type is wrong. README implies anthropic_api_key is sufficient. claude_code_oauth_token is not clearly documented as the correct credential.

signals.topic: GitHub sends one email per comment instead of one consolidated review email — notification spam regression
signals.summary: After a recent update, the action now sends one email per comment instead of one consolidated email containing all comments, as it did before and as manually performed reviews do.
signals.review_reason: This is a regression that degrades the notification experience significantly — reviewers now receive N emails instead of 1 for a single review. This is a clear UX regression from previous behavior. The 'before' state (consolidated email) and 'after' state (per-comment emails) are well-defined, making this a definite behavioral regression.

source_issues.title: Notifications Change
source_issues.evidence: User expects one consolidated email with all comments (as it previously worked and as manual GitHub reviews behave). After an update, each individual comment now triggers a separate email notification, creating email spam for reviewers.

signals.topic: False positive filtering silently fails due to deprecated model (claude-3-5-haiku-20241022)
signals.summary: The secondary false-positive filtering step uses a deprecated/removed model (claude-3-5-haiku-20241022), causing a 404 error. The feature silently degrades to 'Claude filtering disabled', meaning the false-positive reduction logic never runs for any user. The primary security scan continues but all findings remain unfiltered, leading to security finding fatigue.
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine feature regression: the false-positive filtering logic is completely non-functional for every user because it silently falls back to 'filtering disabled'. Users receive unfiltered findings and may waste time triaging false positives, directly degrading the tool's utility. The silent failure mode is particularly harmful — users may not realize the feature is broken. While only 1 issue is reported, the underlying code path affects all users of this action identically (same hardcoded deprecated model). The issue meets the 'key functionality partially unavailable' criterion even though the primary scan still runs.

source_issues.title: False positive filtering fails with 404: claude-3-5-haiku-20241022 model not found
source_issues.evidence: Filter step returns 404 on claude-3-5-haiku-20241022, falls back to 'Claude filtering disabled' with confidence_score: 10.0, keeping all findings unfiltered. The secondary filtering feature is completely non-functional for all users.

signals.topic: Plugin marketplace install strips execute permission from .sh hook scripts, breaking plugin hooks
signals.summary: When plugins are installed via marketplace, .sh files lose their execute bit (755→644), causing all hook scripts to fail with 'Permission denied'. The workaround (chmod +x in ~/.zshrc) is fragile and must be re-applied on every sync. This affects 15+ .sh files across multiple official plugins.
aliases: marketplace install strips +x from shell scripts
signals.review_reason: Three independent reports across macOS/Linux confirm plugin hook scripts fail with 'Permission denied' after marketplace install due to stripped execute bits. This is a core packaging/release defect that directly breaks the plugin hook system (a first-class feature) for users who rely on plugin hooks including official marketplace plugins (ralph-loop, explanatory-output-style). The compounding issue (#40013) shows non-enabled plugins' hooks also fire and fail, meaning every session start generates error noise even for plugins the user deliberately disabled. The only workaround requires a chmod command in ~/.zshrc that reverts on every plugin sync, creating a persistent maintenance burden.

source_issues.title: Plugin system does not preserve execute permission on hook scripts
source_issues.evidence: Hook scripts fail with 'Permission denied' after marketplace install; workaround requires chmod +x in shell profile after every sync

source_issues.title: Plugin marketplace install strips execute permissions from .sh files
source_issues.evidence: 15 .sh files across multiple official plugins (ralph-loop, explanatory-output-style, learning-output-style, math-olympiad, plugin-dev) lose execute bit on install; confirmed via git tree API that source is 100755 but disk copy is 100644

source_issues.title: Hooks from non-enabled marketplace plugins still fire during SessionStart
source_issues.evidence: SessionStart hooks from non-enabled marketplace plugins fire and fail with 'SessionStart:startup hook error' on every session start; compounds the execute bit issue — even if permission were fixed, non-enabled plugins' hooks should not run at all

signals.topic: Keybinding regression: Shift+Enter no longer inserts newline in chat input, breaking standard multiline-input convention
signals.summary: A regression in recent versions removed the Shift+Enter newline binding in the chat input. Users who rely on the standard convention (Enter for newline, Shift+Enter/Cmd+Enter for submit — used in Slack, Discord, and most chat tools) cannot enter multiline messages via keyboard and must use Ctrl+G/Ctrl+E external editor workaround. Additionally, rebinding chat:submit to Shift+Enter leaves the input buffer uncleared after send.
aliases: input buffer not cleared after submit with custom keybindings
signals.review_reason: Two reports (one marked duplicate of the other) confirm a regression where Shift+Enter no longer inserts newlines in chat input, and a secondary bug where custom keybindings for chat:submit leave the input buffer uncleared after send. This breaks the standard multiline-input convention used in every major chat tool (Enter=newline, Shift/Cmd+Enter=submit). The only workaround requires using an external editor (Ctrl+G/Ctrl+E), which is significantly more friction than keyboard shortcuts. Impact is UX-blocking for any user who regularly enters multiline prompts.

source_issues.title: Shift+Enter no longer inserts newline in chat input (default binding missing)
source_issues.evidence: Shift+Enter previously worked as default newline insertion; now does nothing. Workaround of explicit keybinding in ~/.claude/keybindings.json also does not work. Users must use Ctrl+G external editor — significant UX regression for a standard convention used across all major chat tools

source_issues.title: Rebinding chat:submit to shift+enter does not clear input buffer after send
source_issues.evidence: Custom keybinding to make Enter=newline and Shift+Enter=submit (standard Slack/Discord convention) results in submitted text remaining in input buffer after send — broken input buffer management tied to custom keybindings

signals.topic: Telegram plugin: only first permission prompt per session forwarded to Telegram; subsequent prompts silently dropped, blocking multi-step Telegram workflows
signals.summary: The Telegram channel plugin only forwards the first permission prompt per session with Allow/Deny inline keyboard. All subsequent permission prompts are silently dropped — no Telegram notification, terminal blocks waiting for keyboard input. This breaks any Telegram-initiated workflow requiring more than one permission.
aliases: Telegram plugin permission prompt dropped after first
signals.review_reason: Single but highly specific and reproducible report: the Telegram plugin silently drops all permission prompts after the first one per session. Debug logs confirm the first prompt is matched and forwarded, while the second generates no log entry at all. For users running Claude Code via Telegram (a supported channel), any workflow requiring two or more permission-gated actions (e.g., check calendar then delete an event) is completely blocked — the terminal blocks, Telegram user has no way to approve, and there is no error message. This is a silent workflow blocker for a supported integration channel.

source_issues.title: Telegram plugin: only first permission prompt per session is forwarded to Telegram — subsequent prompts are not
source_issues.evidence: First permission prompt correctly forwarded to Telegram with Allow/Deny inline keyboard (confirmed in debug log: 'matched pending'). Second prompt in same session triggers no debug log entry and no Telegram notification — terminal silently blocks waiting for keyboard input with no way for Telegram user to approve

While the issue is labeled 'enhancement' and was closed quickly, the user impact is a hard block on continuing any conversation that has grown large (a common scenario in long Claude Code sessions). The error message should at minimum suggest '/compact' as a recovery action.

signals.topic: Plugin hook shell scripts lose execute bit on install/update, causing Permission denied on every hook trigger
signals.summary: Multiple plugins' .sh hook scripts are shipped without the execute bit, causing 'Permission denied' errors on every session start/exit when the hook fires. This is a recurring failure that blocks hook functionality entirely, requires manual chmod workaround after every plugin update, and affects the core plugin hook mechanism used across the ecosystem.

signals.topic: iMessage plugin SELF detection includes contacts' phone numbers, leaking permission request content to unrelated recipients
signals.summary: The iMessage plugin's self-address detection query (chat.last_addressed_handle) returns recipients' phone numbers alongside the user's own addresses, causing permission request content (bash commands, tool descriptions, raw JSON) to be sent as iMessages to unrelated contacts.
aliases: iMessage SELF address detection includes recipients
permission request sent to wrong contacts
signals.review_reason: Two independent reporters confirm that iMessage plugin's SELF detection uses chat.last_addressed_handle which returns recipients' phone numbers alongside the user's own, causing permission request content (bash commands, tool descriptions, raw JSON) to be sent as iMessages to unrelated contacts. This is a confirmed security and privacy breach — tool permission content is exposed to unintended recipients without user knowledge. In one case, messages were sent to the reporter's mother. This is a direct, harmful consequence for users, not merely a technical inaccuracy.

Privacy concern: reveals Claude Code usage to unintended recipients.

source_issues.evidence: Permission request content including bash commands and tool descriptions sent to user's mother's iMessage chat and potentially other unrelated phone numbers. User had no indication until recipient mentioned it. Security + privacy breach confirmed by reporter.

signals.topic: Telegram plugin in polling mode causes messages to be silently dropped across multiple concurrent Claude Code sessions
signals.summary: Multiple concurrent Claude Code sessions each spawn their own Telegram plugin instance polling via getUpdates; Telegram delivers each update to only one consumer causing messages to be randomly lost. Additionally, the allowed_updates filter set by a previous session persists on Telegram's server, causing message-type updates to be silently dropped even for single-session users.
aliases: Telegram polling causes message loss multi-session
signals.review_reason: Two reports confirm that Telegram plugin silently drops messages in multi-session environments — the dominant real-world usage pattern. The 409 Conflict between competing polling instances causes messages to be delivered to a random session rather than the one the user is actively using. Secondary issue: allowed_updates filter persists server-side, dropping messages even for single-session users. Both are reliability failures where messages are lost with no user notification. Impact is a broken communication channel that appears functional but silently fails.

source_issues.title: Telegram plugin: multiple instances cause 409 conflicts and messages are silently dropped
source_issues.evidence: Up to 5 concurrent bun server.ts processes polling the same bot token observed. Only one instance wins the 409 race, rest spin in retry loop. Messages sent by user consumed by random instance; user at Remote Control session rarely gets response. allowed_updates filter gets stuck on Telegram server causing message updates to be silently dropped even in single-session use.

source_issues.title: Telegram plugin: support webhook mode to fix multi-session message loss
source_issues.evidence: In real-world usage with 5+ concurrent Claude Code sessions, the majority of Telegram messages never reach the active session. Messages are silently dropped with no indication to sender or user. getUpdates polling makes it impossible to run reliable webhook alongside plugin.

signals.topic: Discord plugin DM replies fail after permission prompt due to recipientId lost from channel cache

aliases: Discord DM channel cache recipientId lost
Discord reply fails after permission approval

After a user approves a permission prompt, all subsequent Discord DM replies fail with 'channel not allowlisted' — a main-flow break that silences the user without any indication of why. The allowlist check depends on recipientId which is lost during the notification delivery code path. This blocks the core Discord DM communication loop, leaving users with no response and no error visibility into why.

source_issues.title: Discord: reply fails after permission prompt — recipientId lost from DM channel cache
source_issues.evidence: After permission prompt, fetchAllowedChannel() loses ch.recipientId from cache causing allowlist check to fail. User's sender ID is confirmed in access.json allowFrom list but reply still fails. Confirmed root cause: discord.js re-creates DM channel during user.send() for permission notification, losing recipientId. Repro steps provided with concrete error message.

signals.topic: MCP stdio tool causes SIGSEGV use-after-free crash on ARM64, blocking all MCP tool usage
signals.summary: Goose v1.28.0 on aarch64/ARM64 crashes with SIGSEGV (SEGV_MAPERR) at a poisoned memory address every time it processes a response from a stdio-based MCP extension. The crash is 100% reproducible on every MCP tool call, confirmed via coredumpctl. The faulting address (0x8080808080808087) is a classic use-after-free pattern — memory freed and poisoned by jemalloc, then dereferenced. This completely blocks any MCP stdio extension from functioning on ARM64 hardware.
aliases: use-after-free in MCP response processing ARM64
signals.review_reason: The crash is 100% reproducible and blocks ALL MCP stdio tool usage on ARM64. While count=1, the impact is severe (process termination) and the user provided comprehensive evidence including coredumpctl logs and strace analysis. This is a genuine workflow-blocking crash, not a feature request.

source_issues.title: SIGSEGV (use-after-free) when processing MCP stdio tool response on ARM64
source_issues.evidence: 100% reproducible SIGSEGV on every MCP tool invocation on ARM64, confirmed via coredumpctl (8 consecutive crashes), strace shows poisoned address 0x8080808080808087 indicating use-after-free in MCP response processing path. Exit code 139. MCP server verified working in isolation.

Users cannot use the desktop app at all on fresh install.

signals.topic: ACP provider token usage tracking completely broken — cost reporting and context-window monitoring non-functional
signals.summary: When using an ACP backend (claude-acp, codex-acp), Provider::complete() always returns ProviderUsage with all-zero token counts. Token tracking, cost reporting, and context-window monitoring are broken for any ACP-based provider. The root cause is a three-point gap: the AcpUpdate::Complete enum only carries StopReason (no usage), the PromptResponse usage is silently dropped on arrival, and the stream handler never yields ProviderUsage on completion.
signals.review_reason: Billing/cost reporting is a critical user-facing feature that is completely non-functional for all ACP providers. Users have no visibility into token consumption or cost. The issue provides precise root cause analysis of three specific code locations where usage data is discarded.

source_issues.title: fix(acp): ACP client provider discards token usage from PromptResponse
source_issues.evidence: Technical analysis identifies three specific code gaps: enum lacks usage field, usage silently dropped at L1112, stream handler yields nothing on Complete. Users of ACP providers (claude-acp, codex-acp) cannot see token usage, cost, or context-window data. ACP protocol schema v0.10.8 supports usage reporting but Goose drops it.

signals.review_reason: 体验显著下降：输出格式异常导致对话内容逐字显示，严重影响可读性，用户持续受影响且无法正常获取回复内容。

source_issues.title: 输出格式出现问题
source_issues.evidence: User reports that after an unknown event, all subsequent chat outputs display as one character per line after line breaks, with a visual screenshot showing the broken output; multiple comments indicate the issue persists across all conversations

signals.topic: Kanban provider/model configuration UI fails across multiple API providers — blank model dropdowns, duplicate entries, schema crashes, and spurious OAuth errors block agent startup
signals.summary: Multiple Kanban GUI and CLI issues prevent users from configuring API providers: LM Studio model dropdown is blank/incorrect, custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints cannot be configured with duplicate OpenAI entries, the AI SDK schema crashes on tool preparation, and an OCA OAuth session shows spurious re-authentication errors despite an active session.
signals.review_reason: 4 distinct issues all within the Kanban provider configuration subsystem. Each has direct user impact evidence: agents fail to start, tasks cannot be submitted, or the CLI crashes outright. The multiplicity across LM Studio, custom OpenAI-compatible, OCA OAuth, and AI SDK schema types indicates a systemic problem in the Kanban provider initialization path. Count=4 meets P0 threshold.

source_issues.title: GUI configuration shows blank/incorrect models from LM Studio API on Windows 11
source_issues.evidence: Model selection dropdown is blank or shows incorrect suggestions for LM Studio provider. Users must manually edit providers.json. Agent tasks fail with 'Invalid model identifier'. Only 1 comment (no resolution).

source_issues.title: Kanban cannot configure custom API service providers that are OpenAI-compatible, and there are two 'OpenAI' options in the dropdown list
source_issues.evidence: Kanban GUI dropdown shows duplicate 'OpenAI' entries and cannot configure custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints. Users cannot set up working custom providers through the UI.

source_issues.title: Cline Kanban CLI: TypeError: schema is not a function in @ai-sdk/provider-utils
source_issues.evidence: Kanban CLI crashes with TypeError: schema is not a function during tool preparation in @ai-sdk/provider-utils. The Kanban CLI fails to start and process any agent tasks. Full stack trace provided.

source_issues.title: Kanban Agent fails with OCA OAuth re-authentication error despite active session
source_issues.evidence: Kanban Agent shows 'OAuth session for oca requires re-authentication' despite Settings displaying an active session with ~1 hour remaining. Every prompt fails with this error, blocking the agent workflow.

signals.topic: AI assistant deletes files when file write operations are interrupted or exceed ~400 lines — data loss with no recovery path
signals.summary: When AI assistant performs file operations that either exceed approximately 400 lines or are interrupted (user cancellation, API errors, system hangs), the target files are deleted instead of being preserved or properly written. The deleted files are not recoverable from git if never committed.
aliases: File deleted instead of preserved on write failure
signals.review_reason: Data loss is a critical user harm even at count=1. The issue documents irreversible file deletion with a clear reproducible pattern (files >400 lines, interrupted operations). No workaround available; git cannot recover uncommitted deleted files. Priority is P1 (not P0) because it is single-report and not platform-wide, but the severity of data loss justifies P1 over P2.

source_issues.title: AI Assistant Deletes Files When File Operations Are Interrupted or Exceed 400 Lines
source_issues.evidence: Files are deleted instead of preserved when write fails or operation is interrupted. User lost an 800+ line src/codegen.rs file that was never committed (not recoverable from git). Pattern: every attempt to write >400 lines fails and deletes the file. Root causes identified: no chunking, no atomic writes, no rollback on interruption, poor error handling.

signals.topic: npm global install of Cline CLI fails on macOS ARM64 due to sharp native module build failure — blocks all usage on Apple Silicon
signals.summary: Running `npm i -g cline` on macOS with ARM64 architecture fails because the transitive dependency sharp@0.34.5 (via ink-picture) cannot find prebuilt binaries and fails to build from source, requiring node-addon-api which is absent from the dependency tree.
aliases: Global install fails on Apple Silicon
sharp build error on macOS ARM64
npm i -g cline broken on darwin arm64
signals.review_reason: Complete install failure on macOS ARM64 is a significant user-blocking issue. While count=1, Apple Silicon is the dominant macOS architecture, making this a high-impact blocker. No resolution provided; workaround requires manual steps. P1 appropriate as it is not cross-platform or multi-symptom.

source_issues.title: npm i -g cline fails on macOS arm64 — sharp build error via ink-picture
source_issues.evidence: Global install of cline fails completely on macOS ARM64 (Apple Silicon) due to sharp@0.34.5 build failure. npm errors during node-gyp build. Requires manual workaround (ignore-scripts + platform-specific sharp binary). Affects both Node.js v22 and v24. No resolution in comments.

signals.topic: stdio MCP servers launched with cwd=/ instead of workspace root — breaks project-context-dependent MCP servers
signals.summary: When Cline launches a stdio MCP server, the process is started with working directory set to / (root) instead of the currently opened workspace root. This causes MCP servers that depend on project context to fail silently or with initialization errors.
aliases: MCP server launched from root directory
MCP server fails because not in project directory
signals.review_reason: MCP server functionality is broken by a single misconfiguration (wrong cwd). The issue is well-documented with evidence that the MCP server works correctly outside Cline. Silent failure mode (no clear error pointing to cwd) makes this hard for users to diagnose. P1 as it blocks a key extensibility feature.

source_issues.title: Cline MCP cwd Issue
source_issues.evidence: stdio MCP server (cocoindex-code) launched with cwd=/ and no workspace environment variables. MCP server fails with 'Not in an initialized project directory' error and closes connection. User verified the MCP server works correctly outside of Cline with proper cwd. No workspace-related env vars present. Affects any MCP server needing project context.

signals.topic: Cline ACP protocol fails to initialize in JetBrains IDEs — agent immediately terminates with internal error
signals.summary: When Cline is used through ACP (Agent Client Protocol) in JetBrains IDEs, the ACP session immediately terminates with an internal error. The process exits with code 143.
signals.review_reason: ACP protocol is a core integration path for using Cline in JetBrains. Complete failure to initialize means the entire use case is blocked. Though count=1, the impact is a complete feature outage for an entire IDE platform. P1 is appropriate.

source_issues.title: Unable to use Cline via ACP in JetBrains IDEs
source_issues.evidence: ACP session for Cline in JetBrains IDEs fails immediately with 'Failed to initialize ACP session. Error: Internal error' and process terminates with exit code 143. Reproduced on both v3.67.0 and v3.75.0. Full JsonRpc error stack trace provided.

signals.topic: Model API errors causing main workflow failures (400/401/404/network)
signals.summary: Multiple model API errors across providers block the main chat workflow: a 404 for a deprecated/misnamed Claude model (#11925), a 401 for an invalid OpenAI API key (#11921), a 400 tool-use protocol error on Claude Opus 4.6 (#11929), and a proxy connection failure to OpenAI (#11933). All manifest as direct workflow-blocking API errors with no fallback.
signals.review_reason: Four API errors from distinct root causes (deprecated model name, bad credentials, tool protocol violation, proxy misconfiguration) all result in the same outcome: the user's main chat workflow is completely blocked with no graceful degradation. The 404 and 400 errors in particular suggest bugs within Continue's provider integration code, not just external factors.

source_issues.title: Error: Claude 3.5 Sonnet - 404
source_issues.evidence: API returns 404 'model: claude-4-sonnet' — likely Continue sending a deprecated or renamed model name to the Anthropic provider, blocking the entire chat workflow

source_issues.title: Error: GPT-5 - 401
source_issues.evidence: API key flagged as incorrect: 'Incorrect API key provided' — could indicate Continue mishandling or corrupting API keys in transit

source_issues.title: Error: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M Beta) - 400
source_issues.evidence: 400 BadRequestError: model returned tool_use blocks without corresponding tool_result — a protocol/state tracking bug in Continue's tool orchestration causing the workflow to fail

source_issues.title: Error: GPT-5 - Unknown error
source_issues.evidence: Proxy connection failure: 'Failed to establish a socket connection to proxies: PROXY 10.52.64.215:44355' — network/proxy configuration issue preventing API access

signals.topic: API rate limit / quota exceeded blocking paying users mid-session
signals.summary: Users reported being blocked by API usage limits or quota exceeded errors on Anthropic (issue #11934), Gemini (issue #11926), and OpenAI (issue #11900) providers. In #11934, a paying per-token user is blocked until 2026-04-01, explicitly complaining about being charged per token but having their usage cut off — a clear billing-while-blocked anti-pattern.
signals.review_reason: Three distinct users across three different providers (Anthropic, Gemini, OpenAI) are blocked from using the product due to rate limits/quota. #11934 is particularly significant: a paying per-token user is blocked until a future date, which represents a direct cost-loss scenario where billing continues while the core product is unusable.

source_issues.title: Error: OpenAI GPT-4.1 - 429
