signals.topic: Tool execution failures — local Ollama model and chat agent file editing broken
signals.summary: Two separate tool execution breakdowns: #11879 (closed) is a regression where a previously working Ollama qwen3.5 9b model lost the ability to execute tools, with the model responding it 'cannot access' the file system; #11818 reports the AI chat agent frequently fails to edit files and tool calls consistently fail. Both represent core functionality breakdown.
signals.review_reason: Tool execution is the primary value proposition of Continue as an AI code agent. #11879 is explicitly a regression (user states 'it was working last week') meaning a previously functional setup is now completely broken. #11818 confirms file editing and tool calls 'frequently' fail in the chat agent. Together they indicate a systemic tool execution reliability problem.

source_issues.title: Tools no longer work
source_issues.evidence: User reports tools worked last week with Ollama qwen3.5 9b but now fail: model states 'I cannot directly access your local file system' and 'do not have rights to read files.' Clear regression — previously working local tool execution now completely broken.

source_issues.title: ai chat error
source_issues.evidence: User reports 'The agent often fails to edit files, and tool calls frequently fail.' Accompanied by screenshot evidence showing the error UI. Two comments indicate ongoing discussion.

signals.topic: Windows prompt file parsing broken — home directory prompts unparsed and CRLF EOL causing full file dump
signals.summary: Two Windows-specific prompt file parsing bugs: #11882 — prompts placed in ~/.continue/prompts/ are detected and listed in slash commands but load as empty content (the file is not parsed); #11876 — prompt files with CRLF line endings cause the entire raw markdown file content to be displayed instead of the parsed prompt name/description. Both are documented bugs that break the prompt workflow on Windows.
aliases: home directory prompt files not loading
signals.review_reason: Two distinct but Windows-related prompt file parsing failures that prevent users from using custom prompts as designed. The CRLF issue (#11876) is particularly problematic because Windows defaults to CRLF, meaning new Windows users will encounter this immediately. The home directory issue (#11882) breaks a documented configuration path. Both have clear reproduction steps and screenshots.

source_issues.title: Prompt files in User HOME ~/.continue/prompts directory not being parsed in Windows
source_issues.evidence: Continue detects prompt files in ~/.continue/prompts/ and shows filenames in slash command candidates, but selecting them results in empty/unparsed content. Workaround is using the project-level .continue/prompts directory instead.

source_issues.title: Continue fails to parse prompts.md file when EOL sequence is CRLF
source_issues.evidence: When prompt files use CRLF line endings (Windows default), the entire raw markdown file is shown instead of the parsed name/description. Switching to LF EOL fixes the issue. Screenshots demonstrate the bug clearly.

signals.topic: MCP server reconnection race condition — SSE/STDIO transports fail on reload
signals.summary: When reconnecting an MCP server (via reload or disable/enable), Continue throws 'Already connected to a transport. Call close() before connecting to a new transport' and fails to reconnect. Root cause identified in MCPConnection.ts: the same Client instance is reused across reconnections while _transport is not cleared synchronously, causing a race condition. Affects SSE, STDIO, and HTTP→SSE fallback transports.
signals.review_reason: MCP server reconnection is a common operation (user pressing reload or restarting a server). The race condition means the MCP server becomes permanently stuck in a broken state after the first reload, with no recovery path except reconfiguring from scratch. Clear reproduction steps, identified root cause, and a fix PR (#11887) confirm this is a genuine and significant bug.

source_issues.title: MCP STDIO transport reconnection race condition causes inconsistent state
source_issues.evidence: Bug report includes full root cause analysis: same Client instance reused, _transport not cleared synchronously. PR #11887 exists with fix. Initial connection succeeds, but any subsequent reconnection fails. Affects SSE, STDIO, and HTTP→SSE auto-detect fallback.

signals.topic: LLM truncation detection failure — stop_reason silently discarded
signals.summary: The stop_reason field from Anthropic API responses is permanently discarded before reaching any hook, callback, or event subscriber, causing silent truncation with no user-detectable signal.
signals.review_reason: User pain point — main flow silent failure: truncation produces incomplete data with zero user-visible signal. The response is permanently discarded before reaching any hook, making programmatic detection impossible. User reported significant downstream data corruption in the final synthesis path.

source_issues.title: AnthropicCompletion._handle_completion silently discards stop_reason; no way to detect truncation via hooks or events
source_issues.evidence: stop_reason field is accessible in _handle_completion() and _handle_tool_use_conversation() but never read; truncation signal permanently lost; downstream data corruption reported by user in final synthesis response path.

signals.topic: Shared LLM stop words accumulate across agents causing premature termination
signals.summary: When agents share an LLM instance, stop words added by one agent mutate the shared object and persist for subsequent agents, leading to premature LLM termination and silently wrong outputs.
signals.review_reason: User pain point — main flow silent failure: shared LLM mutation causes wrong outputs with no error thrown. Affects all multi-agent crews sharing LLM instances (the common pattern). Premature termination is silent, making it hard to diagnose.

source_issues.title: Shared LLM `stop` parameter mutation — stop words accumulate across agents
source_issues.evidence: stop words added by agent A persist in shared LLM instance; agent B inherits accumulated stop words and terminates prematurely; silent wrong outputs result with no error; race condition in async multi-agent crews.

signals.topic: Multi-provider LLM routing fails with AuthenticationError due to base_url/api_base mismatch
signals.summary: When using litellm with custom providers (Scaleway, Nebius), LLM calls fail with AuthenticationError because base_url is not mapped to api_base, breaking multi-provider setups.
signals.review_reason: User pain point — main flow blocking: LLM calls fail entirely with AuthenticationError in multi-provider setups. Breaks real production configurations (Scaleway + Nebius). Agent internals bypass LLM object params, making workarounds non-viable.

source_issues.title: liteLLM multi-provider routing fails — base_url not mapped to api_base
source_issues.evidence: LLM calls fail with AuthenticationError when using custom endpoints; base_url not mapped to api_base parameter; global env vars cannot serve both standard and custom endpoints simultaneously; agent internals bypass LLM object params entirely.

signals.topic: TextFile input causes ValueError on non-vision models (regression from v1.10)
signals.summary: Passing TextFile via input_files parameter raises ValueError on non-vision models even though the file is text-only. This is a regression that blocks existing workflows.
signals.review_reason: User pain point — breaking regression: existing workflows fail with ValueError after upgrading to v1.10. Text-only files incorrectly require vision-capable models, forcing users to downgrade or change their working configuration.

source_issues.title: TextFile causes error when used with non-multimodal models
source_issues.evidence: Passing TextFile via input_files raises ValueError on non-vision models (e.g. claude-sonnet-4-6); text-only file incorrectly requires multimodal model; regression from version 1.10; blocks existing text-only workflows.

signals.topic: MCP tool resolver silent failure — UnboundLocalError crash when zero tools discovered
signals.summary: MCPToolResolver._resolve_native() silently returns an empty tool list causing an UnboundLocalError crash with no warning logged, making it impossible to diagnose why MCP server tools are unavailable.
signals.review_reason: User pain point — main flow crash: MCP tool resolution crashes with UnboundLocalError when zero tools are discovered. No diagnostic warning is logged, leaving users unable to identify why their MCP server integration is broken.

source_issues.title: MCPToolResolver._resolve_native() causes UnboundLocalError when tools list is empty
source_issues.evidence: MCPToolResolver._resolve_native() returns empty tool list when no tools discovered; causes UnboundLocalError at tool_resolver.py line 412; no warning logged; users cannot diagnose why MCP server provides no tools.

signals.topic: Gemini CLI crashes with JavaScript heap out of memory after extended idle/waiting period
signals.summary: CLI crashes with FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit / JavaScript heap out of memory after the user leaves the session idle for an extended period (waiting on a reply). The process exhausts ~4GB heap and terminates, losing all session state and work in progress.
signals.review_reason: Direct crash with complete stack trace evidence. User loses entire session state and in-progress work. Marked as possible-duplicate indicating this is a recurring issue. The heap grows to 56GB before OOM, indicating a memory leak in the idle/waiting state path.

source_issues.title: Random crash
source_issues.evidence: Stack trace shows FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory. GC logs show 56GB memory usage before crash. User left machine idle waiting on a reply and returned to find the process had crashed.

signals.topic: Silent model fallback on MODEL_CAPACITY_EXHAUSTED (429) corrupts user workflow without warning
signals.summary: When a user explicitly pins a model (e.g., gemini-3.1-pro-preview) and the backend returns 429 MODEL_CAPACITY_EXHAUSTED, the CLI silently falls back to Flash instead of surfacing the error. This corrupts the ongoing context since Pro and Flash have different reasoning/formatting, and the error is only visible in the F12 debug console — making it appear the requested model succeeded.
signals.review_reason: Workflow corruption with explicit user-witnessed evidence. The CLI silently substitutes a fundamentally different model (Pro vs Flash) without any terminal-visible warning, producing incorrect output the user cannot trust. The possible-duplicate label links to 10+ prior instances across the codebase, confirming this is a high-frequency recurring pattern, not an isolated incident. This constitutes a deceptive failure mode where the CLI appears to succeed while delivering wrong results.

source_issues.title: [Bug/UX] Critical Workflow Corruption: Silent Model Fallback on MODEL_CAPACITY_EXHAUSTED (429)
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly pinned gemini-3.1-pro-preview with 31% quota remaining. Backend returned 429 MODEL_CAPACITY_EXHAUSTED. CLI silently fell back to Flash model, corrupting workflow context. Error buried in F12 debug console only. Marked as possible-duplicate linking to #23986, #23362, #19911, #12216, #22648, #15186, #22545, #22639, #23980, #10722 — indicating a widespread recurring pattern.

signals.topic: ACP mode drops responses and merges answers across sequential prompts, blocking persistent session use
signals.summary: When using gemini --acp (Agent Client Protocol) for programmatic/stdio integration, sequential session/prompt calls within the same session exhibit two correlated failures: (1) prompts 2+ return empty end_turn with no agent_message_chunk, and (2) the missing response text gets appended to a later prompt's response. This prevents ACP from functioning as a persistent server, which is its primary use case.
signals.review_reason: Blocking workflow failure for the ACP integration use case. The first prompt succeeds but prompts 2+ hang indefinitely (60s timeout), and responses get silently merged — making the CLI unreliable for programmatic use. The primary ACP use case (persistent server for sequential requests to avoid startup overhead) is completely broken. Full reproduction script provided, ruling out user environment issues.

source_issues.title: ACP mode: session/prompt drops responses and merges answers across sequential prompts
source_issues.evidence: Full reproduction script in Python demonstrates Prompt 1 returns 'PONG', Prompt 2 returns '' (timeout at 60s), Prompt 3 returns 'PINGHELLO' (merged from prompts 2+3). First prompt in a session always works; issue manifests on 2nd+ prompts. User-impacting: ACP cannot function as a persistent server for sequential requests, forcing users to incur ~7s CLI startup overhead per request.

signals.topic: MCP client remains connected after stopping extension due to incorrect client key lookup in stopExtension()
signals.summary: McpClientManager.stopExtension() removes extension-backed MCP servers from allServerConfigs but does not properly disconnect the running client. The implementation passes the MCP server name instead of the computed client key to disconnectClient(), leaving the backing MCP client connected while the extension appears unloaded in config state. This causes state inconsistency and may prevent proper extension lifecycle management.
aliases: extension stop does not disconnect MCP client
signals.review_reason: Functional bug with clear user-visible state inconsistency. The extension appears unloaded to the user but its MCP client remains running in the background, leading to resource leaks, unexpected behavior on re-enablement, and potential security implications (client stays authenticated after apparent uninstall). The code path is clearly traceable to a key mismatch bug.

source_issues.title: McpClientManager.stopExtension does not disconnect extension-backed MCP clients
source_issues.evidence: Code analysis shows disconnectClient() expects the computed client key but stopExtension() passes the MCP server name. Extension appears unloaded in config state while the backing MCP client remains connected, creating state inconsistency.

signals.topic: Permission flag blocked on cloud GPU environments (RunPod/Lambda/Vast.ai root-only) — autonomous loop fails
signals.summary: On most GPU cloud platforms (RunPod, Lambda, Vast.ai, etc.), containers run as root by default. Claude Code's `--dangerously-skip-permissions` flag is blocked when running as root for security reasons, making the autonomous research loop impossible. The agent stops every 2–3 minutes waiting for human approval, consuming 16 hours of compute with only 3 real experiment results.
aliases: RunPod root user autonomous loop failure
signals.review_reason: This is a primary-flow blocking issue. Autoresearch's core value proposition is fully autonomous hyperparameter search, but the main permission flag required for that is systematically blocked on all common GPU cloud infrastructure. The issue provides specific quantitative evidence: 16 hours of H100 compute wasted with only ~3 valid results, demonstrating direct cost loss and workflow failure.

source_issues.title: --dangerously-skip-permissions blocked on RunPod (root-only environments)
source_issues.evidence: Agent stops every 2-3 minutes for permission prompts. User spent 16 hours with only ~3 real experiment results on H100 80GB. All common GPU cloud providers run root-only. No workaround available without fragile manual steps.

signals.topic: Editable pip install fails due to setuptools flat-layout ambiguity
signals.summary: Running `uv pip install -e .` or `pip install -e .` fails with 'Multiple top-level modules discovered in a flat-layout: [train, prepare]' error, blocking local development and extension of the project.
signals.review_reason: This is a developer-experience blocker for anyone wanting to extend or modify the project locally. It fails on a clean install command that is the standard Python development workflow. The issue is reproducible on both uv and pip, and the error is reproducible in standard environments.

source_issues.title: Editable install fails due to multiple top-level modules (setuptools discovery issue)
source_issues.evidence: Clean reproduction provided: 'uv pip install -e .' and 'pip install -e .' both fail with the same error. Affects both uv and pip on Linux (HPC cluster). Temporary fix identified but requires manual pyproject.toml modification.

signals.topic: Claude agent repeatedly asks permission questions, blocking autonomous execution even after prompt configuration
signals.summary: When using Claude as the agent backend, Claude Code repeatedly asks permission questions (e.g., 'Do you want to proceed?', 'Do you want to add it to a log?') every few minutes during autonomous execution. Adding instruction prompts to program.pd telling Claude not to ask questions has no effect, causing the autonomous loop to break repeatedly.
signals.review_reason: This is an autonomous execution blocker. The agent repeatedly stops mid-workflow to ask for human approval, which directly contradicts the core autonomous research loop functionality. The workaround (program.pd prompt) is explicitly documented and fails, leaving users with no reliable solution. It is distinct from issue #396 (permission flag blocked) because it occurs even when not running as root.

source_issues.title: Claude always ask questions while running
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly added prompt 'You have full permission of creating logs of models. Do not ask me any more questions. Please continue autonomously with no questions.' to program.pd, but Claude still repeatedly asks permission questions every few minutes, breaking the autonomous loop.

signals.topic: analysis.ipynb crashes with UnboundLocalError/NameError due to 'best' variable used before definition
signals.summary: The analysis.ipynb notebook has a cell that references the 'best' variable before it is defined in a later cell, causing an UnboundLocalError or NameError when cells are run sequentially.
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed crash that prevents users from running the analysis notebook, which is part of the project's standard workflow for reviewing experiment results. The bug is explicitly labeled 'bug' and has a prepared fix, confirming the defect. However, it is low-frequency impact (notebook analysis is a post-processing step, not the core autonomous loop) and affects only a single workflow.

source_issues.title: Bug: 'best' variable used before definition in analysis.ipynb
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed bug with labeled 'bug' tag. Variable 'best' is used to calculate margin and set y-axis limits in one cell but defined in a later cell. Triggers UnboundLocalError or NameError when notebook cells run sequentially. Reporter has prepared a fix.

signals.topic: Codex agent backend ignores 'never stop' instruction, preventing autonomous operation with alternative agents
signals.summary: Codex does not work with autoresearch because it ignores the instruction to never stop and keeps pausing for user input, unlike Claude which respects this instruction. This limits users who prefer or need to use Codex as their agent backend.
signals.review_reason: This is a key functional limitation: alternative agent backends (specifically Codex) fail to respect the 'never stop' instruction required for autonomous operation, limiting user choice and forcing reliance on Claude. While opened by the repo owner rather than an external user, it reflects a real architectural constraint that prevents multi-agent flexibility. The 31-comment discussion thread confirms active community interest.

source_issues.title: Codex doesn't seem to work?
source_issues.evidence: Repo owner (karpathy) reports that Codex ignores the instruction to never stop, unlike Claude which supports '/loop'. This makes Codex unusable as the agent backend for autonomous research loops. Active discussion with 31 comments indicates this is a recognized limitation.

signals.topic: AGENTS.md symlink causes unhandled OSError(ELOOP) crash instead of graceful error
signals.summary: When AGENTS.md is a symlink, FilesystemBackend rejects it via O_NOFOLLOW for security, but the resulting OSError(ELOOP) is not handled by _map_exception_to_standard_error, causing an unhandled crash during MemoryMiddleware.before_agent instead of a user-facing error.
signals.review_reason: 主流程失败：symlink场景（常见于CLAUDE.md+AGENTS.md的兼容模式）导致CLI直接崩溃而非优雅报错。虽然是安全加固导致的副作用，但用户无法在symlink场景下使用工具。count=2，有两条独立issue支撑，属于P1级别。

source_issues.title: OSError when AGENTS.md is a symbolic link
source_issues.evidence: CLI crashes with OSError when AGENTS.md is a symlink (e.g., ln -s CLAUDE.md AGENTS.md for Claude Code compatibility). Error: 'OSError: [Errno 40] Too many levels of symbolic links'. Workaround requires replacing symlink with a regular file copy.

source_issues.title: Classify `OSError(ELOOP)` in `FilesystemBackend` error handling
source_issues.evidence: Same root cause as #2245: O_NOFOLLOW rejects symlinks, OSError(ELOOP) not mapped in _map_exception_to_standard_error, causing unhandled crash during MemoryMiddleware.before_agent instead of a user-facing error.

signals.topic: CompiledSubAgent with custom StateGraph causes infinite loop when last message is ToolMessage
signals.summary: When a CompiledSubAgent uses a custom StateGraph that ends with a ToolMessage, the parent agent enters an infinite loop, re-invoking the subagent indefinitely. Root cause: _return_command_with_state_update assumes last message is always an AIMessage, so custom StateGraph subagents never signal completion.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：用户调用CompiledSubAgent + custom StateGraph时，agent无限循环，任务永远无法完成。这直接阻断了使用自定义子智能体的工作流，是P0级别的主流程失败。提供了完整复现代码和根因分析，用户影响明确。

source_issues.title: CompiledSubAgent with custom StateGraph causes infinite loop when last message is ToolMessage
source_issues.evidence: Agent enters infinite loop: 'No explicit error is raised. The agent enters an infinite loop, repeatedly re-invoking the subagent because the parent agent's termination condition is never satisfied.' Root cause identified in subagents.py line 414: _return_command_with_state_update assumes last message is always AIMessage.

signals.topic: GraphLoadError on Windows: server fails to start due to temp module import path
signals.summary: On Windows, deepagents-cli server fails to start with ModuleNotFoundError when importing a server_graph.py file from a temp directory path containing backslashes. The import module path 'C:\Users\...\server_graph' is not treated as a valid module name by Python's importlib.

source_issues.title: GraphLoadError: No module named 'C:\\Users\\...\\server_graph' on Windows (temp server_graph.py)

signals.topic: SummarizationMiddleware token counter misidentifies ChatAnthropicVertex model type, causing incorrect token estimation and middleware never triggering

source_issues.title: _get_approximate_token_counter doesn't recognize ChatAnthropicVertex, causing SummarizationMiddleware to never trigger
source_issues.evidence: Token counter uses hardcoded 'anthropic-chat' type check; ChatAnthropicVertex returns 'anthropic-chat-vertexai'. Middleware silently fails — estimate off by ~32K tokens on 600K input. Reproducible with code sample provided.

OpenAI image block converter drops detail

source_issues.title: convert_to_openai_image_block drops the 'detail' field for image content blocks
source_issues.evidence: Test case shows all permutations of detail field location (top-level, extras dict, metadata dict) are lost in output. User provided parameterized pytest test cases covering url and base64 image sources.

signals.topic: Agent with structured output fails with JSONDecodeError when OpenAI returns phased response (commentary + final_answer)

aliases: structured output phased response parsing failure

source_issues.title: Agent with structured output fails when OpenAI response has phased response with 'commentary' and 'final_answer'
source_issues.evidence: JSONDecodeError 'Extra data: line 1 column 28 (char 27)' raised when parsing AIMessage with multiple phase text items. Minimal repro provided. Occurs with OpenAI phased/streaming structured output.

signals.topic: Pydantic AttributeError crash in SummarizationMiddleware when accessing 'profile' attribute on models with import errors
signals.summary: SummarizationMiddleware raises AttributeError 'ImportErrorProfileModel object has no attribute profile' when the underlying model raises an AttributeError on 'profile' access, due to Pydantic 2's __getattr__ chain swallowing the original error and masking the real cause.
signals.review_reason: Pydantic 2兼容性问题导致中间件启动崩溃，影响特定模型配置用户。有完整测试用例和堆栈，属于langchain-core/langchain关键路径。

source_issues.title: AttributeError: 'ImportErrorProfileModel' object has no attribute 'profile'
source_issues.evidence: Unit test reproduces crash with custom model that raises AttributeError on 'profile' access. Stack trace shows Pydantic 2 __getattr__ re-wrapping the error. Test fails on langchain 1.2.13 / langchain-core 1.2.22 / Python 3.14.

signals.topic: AsyncPostgresSaver/AsyncPostgresStore production connection reliability — idle timeout failures and async lock contention
signals.summary: AsyncPostgresSaver and AsyncPostgresStore have multiple connection/pooling issues causing production failures: missing pool_config support causes psycopg.OperationalError after DB idle timeout (#7304), threading.Lock() serializes all async operations reducing throughput under concurrent load (#7259), and abatch double-checks connections from the pool wasting resources (#7218).
signals.review_reason: Three separate but related issues (#7304, #7259, #7218) all affect the same async Postgres checkpointing path in production. Issue #7304 causes hard production failures (connection closed errors after idle timeout) with no user-configurable workaround. Issue #7259 demonstrably reduces throughput and increases latency under concurrent async load (500-user benchmark cited). Issue #7218 causes connection pool exhaustion risk. All have explicit user impact evidence.

source_issues.title: feat: Add pool_config support to AsyncPostgresSaver.from_conn_string()
source_issues.evidence: AsyncPostgresSaver creates connections not automatically recycled. After DB idle timeout fires, all checkpoint operations fail with psycopg.OperationalError: the connection is closed. No way to configure max_idle, max_lifetime, reconnect_timeout.

source_issues.title: AsyncPostgresSaver enforces instance-level threading.Lock() during asynchronous execution
source_issues.evidence: Python threading.Lock() serializes all asyncio tasks within the same process, preventing full utilization of the underlying psycopg_pool.AsyncConnectionPool. Benchmark shows throughput and latency severely bottlenecked by the lock rather than pool/database capacity.

source_issues.title: AsyncPostgresStore.abatch acquires unused connection and double-checks out from pool
source_issues.evidence: abatch acquires a connection via _ainternal.get_connection but never uses it; _cursor acquires a second connection for all actual I/O. Two connections checked out from pool per call, only one used for real work — wastes connection pool resources.

signals.topic: SqliteSaver.list() N+1 query pattern causes linear performance degradation
signals.summary: SqliteSaver.list() and AsyncSqliteSaver.alist() execute a separate writes query for every checkpoint row returned — a classic N+1 pattern. With 100 checkpoints, 101 queries execute instead of 2, causing performance to degrade linearly with checkpoint count.
signals.review_reason: N+1 query anti-pattern is a confirmed performance regression that worsens with usage scale. User provided a reproducible benchmark with exact query counts. While affecting a single storage backend, checkpoint listing is a high-frequency operation — linear degradation makes long-running graph sessions progressively slower.

source_issues.title: perf(checkpoint-sqlite): N+1 query pattern in SqliteSaver.list() and AsyncSqliteSaver.alist()
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction case shows 101 queries executed for 100 checkpoints instead of 2. Linear degradation confirmed: each checkpoint triggers one additional writes query. User-provided measurable proof with code to reproduce.

signals.topic: add_messages(format='langchain-openai') silently drops message IDs and additional_kwargs
signals.summary: When calling add_messages with format='langchain-openai', message IDs are silently set to None and custom additional_kwargs are silently dropped without any error or warning. This causes silent data loss in OpenAI-compatible workflows.
signals.review_reason: Silent data loss is a high-impact bug. Message IDs are critical for tracking, deduplication, and OpenAI compatibility. additional_kwargs dropping can break tools that depend on message metadata. No error raised makes this especially dangerous — users may not notice until downstream systems fail.

source_issues.title: bug: add_messages(format='langchain-openai') strips message IDs and additional_kwargs
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction case shows HumanMessage id='msg-1' becomes None after add_messages, and AIMessage additional_kwargs={'widgets': [...]} becomes {}. No error raised — data silently lost.

signals.topic: Docker Compose hardcoded postgres:postgres default credential — security risk
signals.summary: LangGraph CLI generates Docker Compose configurations with hardcoded postgres:postgres credentials. Users deploying without customization have a predictable database credential exposed across all orchestrator, API, and executor services.
signals.review_reason: Hardcoded default credentials in generated configurations is a documented security anti-pattern. If users deploy the default Docker Compose config (a common workflow), the database is accessible with a publicly known credential. While not a runtime exploit in the library code itself, the CLI actively generates insecure configurations.

source_issues.title: Suggest: generate random Postgres password instead of hardcoded default in Docker Compose
source_issues.evidence: Hardcoded postgres:postgres URI injected into Docker Compose environment for orchestrator, API, and executor services. Predictable credential exposed if user deploys without customization. Proposed fix is to generate a random password at langgraph up time.

signals.topic: Interrupt resumption on graph replay fails — time travel bug
signals.summary: Resuming interrupts on replay does not work correctly. This breaks the ability to resume a graph from a checkpoint and continue interrupted execution, which is a core LangGraph workflow.
signals.review_reason: Though labeled internal, this is a confirmed bug in the core replay/interrupt-resume workflow — a key LangGraph feature for resuming human-in-the-loop agents from checkpoints. The maintainer-confirmed nature and reference to a fix PR (#7225) provides strong evidence. Breakage of this workflow blocks critical production use cases.

source_issues.title: time travel bug -- resuming interrupts on 'replay'
source_issues.evidence: Privileged issue confirmed by maintainers: resuming interrupts on replay is not working correctly. Referenced PR #7225 addresses the fix. Affects the core checkpoint replay + interrupt resume workflow.

signals.topic: MCP tool integration broken in agent and workflow — wrong input type handling for object/boolean/select
signals.summary: Agent nodes and workflow tool mode incorrectly handle MCP tool inputs: object, boolean, and select types are serialized as strings, causing runtime errors. Workflows that work in Dify 1.8 fail in 1.11+.
signals.review_reason: 3 confirmed issues across agent node, workflow tool mode, and MCP server publish — all sharing the same root cause of incorrect type handling for MCP inputs (object/boolean/select serialized as strings). Regression from v1.8 to v1.11+: workflows that previously worked now fail silently or with type errors at runtime, directly blocking multi-step automation flows.

source_issues.title: MCP input types
source_issues.evidence: Object/boolean/select MCP inputs are treated as strings; workflow errors at runtime with 'expected dict input'. Same issue in workflow tool mode. External MCP clients correctly render the schema.

source_issues.title: agent节点调用mcp服务报错
source_issues.evidence: Same workflow and MCP server work in Dify 1.8 but fail with errors in 1.11.2. Regression introduced between versions.

source_issues.title: agent use mcp bug
source_issues.evidence: Agent node calling MCP service fails in 1.11.2. Error screenshots attached showing type mismatch.

signals.topic: Knowledge base image URLs return container-internal addresses — users cannot view uploaded images
signals.summary: When using S3/MinIO storage, knowledge base image preview URLs expose container-internal paths instead of external URLs, making uploaded images inaccessible to users.
signals.review_reason: Two knowledge base issues from the same user on the same day: image URLs expose container-internal paths (making KB images inaccessible) and recall test returns zero results (making retrieval verification impossible). Both directly prevent core KB functionality — file access and retrieval QA — for self-hosted deployments with S3/MinIO.

source_issues.title: knowledge base image
source_issues.evidence: With S3/MinIO configured, uploaded images return /files/... internal container paths that users cannot access. User explicitly states 'I cannot access this address'.

source_issues.title: The recall test did not show any results
source_issues.evidence: Knowledge base recall test returns no results in Dify 1.13.3 self-hosted. Core RAG retrieval feature is non-functional.

signals.summary: Dify pins the Langfuse SDK to v2.51.3 which lacks LLM-as-judge feature support available in v3+, causing evaluations to fail silently with no scores generated.

source_issues.title: Broken Langfuse LLM-as-judge integration due to outdated SDK pin
source_issues.evidence: SDK pinned at 2.51.3; Langfuse server is v3.161.0. LLM-as-judge evaluations receive observations but produce zero scores. No error is surfaced to the user — silent failure. Explicit user impact: evaluation pipeline is non-functional.

signals.topic: Application blocks / becomes unresponsive during document vectorization
