signals.review_reason: Single report but describes a complete platform freeze — all other applications become unavailable while a document is being vectorized. This is a severe service availability issue for self-hosted deployments, potentially caused by a database lock or worker pool exhaustion. Downgraded to P2 due to count=1, single repo.

source_issues.title: Application blocking
source_issues.evidence: User reports 'other applications unavailable when vectorizing documents, and there is no response after executing for a long time' on Dify 1.13.3 self-hosted. The entire platform becomes unresponsive during document vectorization.

signals.topic: Plugin install fails when dependency download exceeds 120-second timeout
signals.summary: Large plugins fail to install with 'signal: killed' and 'init process exited due to no activity for 120 seconds', making plugins unusable.
signals.review_reason: Single report with detailed logs showing the exact failure point: downloading a 15.8MiB numpy wheel exceeds a hard 120-second timeout, killing the process. Plugin installation is a core extensibility feature — failure prevents entire plugin ecosystem usage.

source_issues.title: plugin install failed
source_issues.evidence: Plugin install fails with 'signal: killed' during numpy download (15.8MiB). Init process exits after 120 seconds of no activity. Large plugins cannot be deployed. Confirmed by 5 comments indicating ongoing discussion.

signals.topic: Node.js SDK ESM/CommonJS `pg` module import crash — all memory operations blocked in ESM environments
signals.summary: Eager `import { Client } from 'pg'` in the ESM bundle causes immediate SyntaxError on module load, blocking all memory operations (add/search/delete) for all users in Node.js ESM mode even when NOT using PostgreSQL/pgvector.
signals.review_reason: Five separate issues across different versions (v2.1.34 to v2.4.2) all confirm the same root cause: `import { Client } from 'pg'` in the ESM bundle. The crash is a hard startup block — module fails to load before any user code runs, completely preventing all memory operations (add/search/delete/get). Users are forced to manually patch the built file as a workaround, and the issue affects any ESM environment (Node.js 22+, OpenClaw plugin, etc.) regardless of whether they use PostgreSQL. This is a main flow block meeting all P0 criteria: count>=3, blocking, with multi-issue evidence spanning multiple versions.

source_issues.title: Node.js SDK: Lazy-load pg to avoid ESM/CJS crash when not using pgvector
source_issues.evidence: Eager import of pg at module load time crashes ESM bundle. All users of OSS Memory class in ESM environments NOT using pgvector are blocked — module crashes before any user code runs.

source_issues.title: [Bug] pgvector ESM import fails in Node.js: Named export 'Client' not found (v2.4.2)
source_issues.evidence: Since v2.4.2 added pgvector support, using pgvector in Node.js ESM context fails immediately on module load with SyntaxError. The ESM bundle uses `import { Client } from 'pg'` but pg is CJS.

source_issues.title: mem0ai OSS: pgvector import breaks under Node ESM (Named export 'Client' not found)
source_issues.evidence: OSS module breaks under Node ESM due to pg CJS import. Same root cause as #4553.

source_issues.title: Bug: SyntaxError - Named export 'Client' not found in pg module (ESM compatibility with Node.js 22)
source_issues.evidence: Breaking change from v0.3.3. Error occurs even when NOT using PostgreSQL — the plugin imports pg regardless. Blocks recall at session bootstrap in OpenClaw.

source_issues.title: openclaw-mem0: memory_store/search fail with pg CommonJS import (Named export 'Client' not found)
source_issues.evidence: Broke memory_store and memory_search in a real OpenClaw runtime. Multiple users affected, local patch required as workaround. Confirmed by reporter that patching to `import pkg from 'pg'; const { Client } = pkg;` fixed it.

signals.topic: Production memory extraction: 97.8% of entries are junk across 32 days of real usage — memory recall is fundamentally unreliable
signals.summary: A systematic production audit of 10,134 memory entries over 32 days with 2 different extraction models showed 97.8% were junk: boot file restating (52.7%), heartbeat/cron noise, hallucinated user profiles, identity confusion, and even security/privacy leaks (IPs, chat IDs, file paths).
aliases: Memory extraction produces mostly junk entries
Noisy memory entries from system prompts
signals.review_reason: A production-grade audit with 10,134 entries measured across 32 days and 2 extraction models constitutes strong, quantified user evidence. The core value proposition of a memory system — reliable recall — is fundamentally broken: 97.8% junk means the agent 'remembers' things it was never told and fails to retain actual facts. Boot-file restating dominates (52.7%), and the model upgrade provided no improvement. This is a systemic quality failure affecting the entire product category, not an edge case. Security/privacy leaks (IPs, file paths, sensitive configs) add data safety risk. The audit quantifies the problem clearly enough to meet P0 standards even at count=1.

source_issues.title: What we found after auditing 10,134 mem0 entries: 97.8% were junk
source_issues.evidence: 32-day production audit across gemma2:2b (20 days) and Claude Sonnet 4.6 (12 days). 97.8% junk rate measured systematically across 10,134 entries. Categories: boot file restating 52.7%, heartbeat/cron noise 11.5%, system architecture dumps 8.2%, hallucinated profiles 5.2%, identity confusion 3.3%, security/privacy leaks 2.1%. Model upgrade did NOT fix it. Only 38 entries out of 10,134 were clean enough to keep.

signals.topic: Fact extraction silently fails on malformed JSON from non-OpenAI LLMs — facts are lost with no retry and no user-visible error
signals.summary: When using non-OpenAI LLMs (Qwen3, Ollama, etc.) for fact extraction, invalid UTF-16 surrogate pair escapes in JSON output cause JSONDecodeError. The exception is caught, logged at ERROR level, and silently sets retrieved facts to empty — all facts from those conversations are lost with no retry.
aliases: UTF-16 surrogate pair escape in JSON
signals.review_reason: Silent data loss is a significant user impact: facts are stored in the system and then vanish with no user notification. Production logs show the error, but users have no visibility into which conversations lost data. The lack of retry means transient LLM failures are not recoverable. This affects any user running non-OpenAI LLMs (Qwen3, Ollama, Cerebras) — a significant and growing use case. The code analysis clearly shows the root cause in _add_to_vector_store, and the production evidence (from a 572-memory deployment) provides concrete impact data.

source_issues.title: Fact extraction silently fails on malformed JSON from non-OpenAI LLMs
source_issues.evidence: Production evidence from Cerebras Qwen3-235B deployment (572 memories). LLM returns HTTP 200 with content, but JSON contains invalid surrogate pairs. Error log: 'Invalid \uXXXX escape: line 1 column 9845'. All facts from those conversations were silently lost with no retry, no user-visible error. Code analysis confirms single try/except catches all exceptions and sets new_retrieved_facts=[].

signals.topic: Fact retrieval crashes on LLM responses with JSON wrapped in explanatory text (no code fences)
signals.summary: When the LLM returns JSON inside explanatory text without markdown code fences, `JSON.parse()` throws an exception and the entire memory operation fails. The code does not defensively extract JSON from the response text before parsing.
aliases: Memory operation crash on non-fenced JSON
signals.review_reason: Memory operation crashes rather than gracefully degrading — the entire addToVectorStore operation fails when the LLM returns text-wrapped JSON. This is a common LLM behavior (explaining results before providing structured output), making it a frequent real-world trigger. The code has a clear fix path (regex extraction before JSON.parse), and the current behavior causes unpredictable failures in production.

source_issues.title: Fact retrieval crashes on LLM responses with JSON wrapped in explanation text (no code fences)
source_issues.evidence: Code analysis shows direct JSON.parse() on LLM response without defensive extraction. When LLM returns 'Here are the facts I extracted:\n{\'facts\': [...]}', JSON.parse throws 'Unexpected token H'. Entire memory operation fails. Proposed fix uses regex to extract JSON object before parsing.

signals.topic: `actor_id` metadata gets overwritten during memory UPDATE operations — breaks actor-level memory isolation in shared workspaces
signals.summary: When Actor B updates a memory created by Actor A, the `actor_id` field is overwritten to Actor B instead of preserving Actor A. This breaks actor-level memory isolation and prevents querying memories by their original creator, affecting shared workspaces, team environments, and multi-player scenarios.
signals.review_reason: Breaks a core feature of the memory system: actor-level memory isolation. In shared user_id scenarios (team workspaces, multi-player games, collaborative agents), the inability to query by original creator after an UPDATE is a fundamental correctness failure. The reporter has done root cause analysis showing the exact faulty condition, and the history table already tracks all contributors — so the proposed fix (preserve original actor_id) is feasible and doesn't lose data.

source_issues.title: Bug Report: `actor_id` metadata gets overwritten during memory UPDATE operations
source_issues.evidence: Root cause analysis in _update_memory() at lines 1251-1252: condition 'actor_id not in new_metadata' always fails because new_metadata always contains current actor's ID (passed from caller via deepcopy). Query by original creator returns 0 results after UPDATE. Breaks core feature (actor isolation) in shared workspaces.

signals.topic: AG-UI session state management failures causing workflow context loss
signals.summary: Multiple AG-UI layer failures cause session state to be lost: MapAGUI() ignores configured session store so every request starts a fresh workflow run; SSE encoding fails for AgentResponseUpdate events (missing model_dump_json attribute); TextContent metadata is silently dropped in AG-UI event stream; and OpenTelemetry traces are not emitted through AGUI.
signals.review_reason: Issue 4920 is a high-severity session state loss: every AG-UI request restarts from scratch, breaking multi-turn conversations in production. Combined with SSE encoding crash (4929), broken text metadata (4923), and missing OTel (4928), four distinct bugs converge on the same core issue: AG-UI layer silently corrupts or loses critical runtime state.

source_issues.title: AG-UI MapAGUI() doesn't use session store or map message AuthorName
source_issues.evidence: MapAGUI() hardcodes session:null when calling aiAgent.RunStreamingAsync() even when session store is configured. Every AG-UI request starts a fresh workflow with no memory. Client must round-trip entire message history each request.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: AG-UI EventEncoder._encode_sse cannot handle AgentResponseUpdate
source_issues.evidence: AttributeError: 'AgentResponseUpdate' object has no attribute 'model_dump_json'. SSE encoding fails for this event type, breaking AG-UI streaming responses.

source_issues.title: .NET: TextContent.AdditionalProperties dropped by AsAGUIEventStreamAsync
source_issues.evidence: TextContent.AdditionalProperties (e.g., textContentType: 'Markdown') is silently dropped when creating TEXT_MESSAGE_START/TEXT_MESSAGE_CONTENT events. AG-UI clients cannot determine how to render text content.

source_issues.title: .NET: [Bug]: OTel is not emitted when invoking agent through AGUI
source_issues.evidence: Despite correctly configuring OpenTelemetry with AddSource for Microsoft.Extensions.AI and Microsoft.Extensions.Agents, no traces are emitted when invoking an agent through AGUI. Complete observability blackout for AG-UI workloads.

signals.topic: MCPStreamableHTTPTool reliability failures causing workflow blocking
signals.summary: MCPStreamableHTTPTool in the Python SDK exhibits two critical reliability bugs: (1) infinite loop when connected to MCP servers that don't implement the 'ping' method (e.g. Snowflake managed MCP), and (2) concurrent request failure where in-flight requests are terminated when one request times out. Additionally, MCP tool binding by reference in declarative YAML is silently ignored, causing 500 errors.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed workflow-blocking bugs: (1) infinite loop completely prevents MCP-based workflows from running on servers without ping support, (2) concurrent request handling silently terminates 4/5 in-flight requests on timeout — production-blocking for multi-user Foundry deployments. Both have clear reproduction paths and code-level root causes.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: MCP client connection goes into infinite loop if MCP server doesn't support ping method
source_issues.evidence: connect=>load_tools=>_ensure_connected=>ping fails=>connect (infinite loop). Blocks any workflow using a Snowflake or similar MCP server without ping support.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: MCPStreamableHTTPTool does not handle Concurrent Requests
source_issues.evidence: When MCP endpoint times out, 4 out of 5 concurrent requests are silently terminated with no response. In-production failure in Foundry Hosted Agent serving via /responses API.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: Support MCP tool binding by reference in declarative YAML
source_issues.evidence: Passing a pre-built MCP tool via `bindings` parameter is silently ignored. MAF constructs the tool from YAML spec regardless, resulting in `server_url: ''` and a 500 error from the API.

signals.topic: .NET chat history management failures causing conversation context loss
signals.summary: Chat history is not maintained correctly across .NET agent workflows: (1) Workflow agents only return the last chat message instead of full history, (2) ChatClientAgent throws an exception when ChatHistoryProvider is used with Azure OpenAI Responses API and store=false, (3) CompactionProvider causes previously persisted messages to be re-added to history even when summarization never triggers.
aliases: chat history provider Azure OpenAI conflict
signals.review_reason: Three independent bugs all cause .NET users to lose or corrupt chat history: (1) workflow agents silently show only the last message, breaking multi-turn memory, (2) combining ChatHistoryProvider with stateless Azure OpenAI requests throws an exception, (3) compaction causes message duplication even when summarization is disabled. All three represent direct user impact on the core conversation memory use case.

source_issues.title: .NET: [Bug]: Unable to get Session chat history in work flow agent
source_issues.evidence: Converting a workflow to AIAgent with a session causes the agent to only show the last message instead of the full chat history. ChatHistoryProvider cannot be added, requiring users to pass the entire message list on every call.

source_issues.title: .NET: [Bug]: ChatClientAgent throws when using ChatHistoryProvider with Azure OpenAI Responses API and store=false
source_issues.evidence: Explicitly setting store=false (stateless request) still causes ChatClientAgent to throw: 'Only ConversationId or ChatHistoryProvider may be used, but not both.' The agent is unusable for stateless Azure OpenAI Responses API calls with a ChatHistoryProvider.

source_issues.title: .NET: [Bug]: CompactionProvider re-adds previously persisted request messages to InMemoryChatHistoryProvider across session round-trips
source_issues.evidence: With InMemoryChatHistoryProvider and CompactionProvider (even when summarization is configured to never run), previously persisted messages are duplicated in chat history after session serialization and reload. User messages appear twice in conversation.

signals.topic: Python handler TypeVar resolution produces confusing downstream errors
signals.summary: Class-based @handler decorator in the Python SDK accepts unresolved TypeVar annotations during registration, but workflow type validation later fails with a TypeCompatibilityError that gives no indication the root cause is an unresolved generic type.
signals.review_reason: While count=1, this is a confirmed bug with a clear follow-up reference to a previous issue (#4534). The error message misdirection is a significant developer experience degradation: users spend time investigating the wrong component (workflow edge validation) when the real issue is in handler type resolution. This is a recurring class of misattribution per the referenced prior issue.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: Raise a clear handler registration error for unresolved TypeVar
source_issues.evidence: Follow-up from issue #4534. Handler registration accepts unresolved TypeVar but failure only surfaces later as TypeCompatibilityError during workflow edge validation. The error points users in the wrong direction, making debugging time-consuming.

signals.topic: New Foundry UI forces accidental agent creation and provides no naming guidance
signals.summary: The New Foundry experience presents users with a 'Create agent' primary action button before the lab guide instructs them to create one, resulting in accidental redundant agent creation. No visible character limit for agent/workflow names causes silent failures, and API key input appears to have reliability issues.
aliases: New Foundry forced agent creation UX
signals.review_reason: Count=1 limits this to P1, but the review_reason provides explicit user impact evidence: accidental creation of multiple resources, silent failure modes for naming, and significant user confusion. This is a UX anti-pattern that actively misleads users into performing unintended actions — a notable experience degradation even for a single report.

source_issues.title: Usability + Reliability Issues in New Foundry (Graphic Agent Framework Lab)
source_issues.evidence: User naturally clicked 'Create agent' primary button in the New Foundry welcome panel, which was already created implicitly. Only way to cancel was a small X in the corner, resulting in accidental creation of multiple agents. No character limit shown for names — long names fail silently. The user had to invest significant effort to understand the unexpected state.

signals.topic: MCP tool poisoning enables arbitrary code execution via unsigned tool definitions — no signature verification or schema pinning
signals.summary: AutoGen's MCP integration fetches tool definitions and executes them without any signature verification, schema pinning, or integrity checks. A compromised or malicious MCP server can inject arbitrary tool instructions or alter tool schemas. Reported with CVE-2025-6514 and a demonstrated 72.8% poisoning success rate. Also lacks per-message authentication, replay protection, and agent identity verification on the MCP channel.
signals.review_reason: Two related issues document a concrete, exploitable vulnerability in AutoGen's MCP integration: tools are fetched and executed without signature verification or schema pinning, and MCP messages carry no authentication or replay protection. CVE-2025-6514 and a 72.8% demonstrated success rate provide credible user-impact evidence. This is not a theoretical risk — compromised MCP servers can achieve arbitrary code execution through poisoned tool definitions.

source_issues.title: MCP tool poisoning can enable arbitrary code execution via unsigned tool definitions
source_issues.evidence: Reports 72.8% tool poisoning success rate, CVE-2025-6514 cited, relates to guardrails epic #6017. Compromised MCP server can inject instructions or change tool schemas.

source_issues.title: MCP tool integration has no per-message authentication or integrity verification
source_issues.evidence: No agent identity, no message signing, no tool integrity verification, no replay protection on MCP integration. References IETF MCP security draft.

signals.topic: SelectorGroupChat livelock when allow_repeated_speaker=False — fallback returns excluded previous speaker
signals.summary: SelectorGroupChat enters a livelock when allow_repeated_speaker=False is set and the LLM-based selector exhausts max_selector_attempts. The fallback logic incorrectly returns self._previous_speaker (the excluded speaker) instead of a valid alternative, causing the group chat to stall.
signals.review_reason: SelectorGroupChat is a core AutoGen orchestration pattern. The bug causes livelock — a complete workflow block — when the LLM selector fails and allow_repeated_speaker=False is set. This is a reproducible, deterministic failure in a main-path feature. The fix is well-scoped (fallback logic) and the issue clearly describes the root cause.

source_issues.title: [Bug] SelectorGroupChat livelock: fallback returns excluded previous speaker when allow_repeated_speaker=False
source_issues.evidence: Bug: when allow_repeated_speaker=False and the LLM-based selector exhausts max_selector_attempts, the fallback returns self._previous_speaker (the excluded speaker), causing livelock. Suggestion: fallback should select a random participant that is NOT the previous speaker.

signals.topic: LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor executes LLM-generated code without sandboxing — UserWarning easily suppressed
signals.summary: LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor writes LLM-generated code to disk and executes it without any sandboxing mechanism. Only a UserWarning is emitted at construction, which is trivially suppressible and easily missed in logs. Severity rated HIGH and mapped to OWASP ASI-09. Users may unknowingly execute arbitrary shell commands on their host.
signals.review_reason: LLM-generated code execution without sandboxing is a high-severity risk that can lead to arbitrary command execution on user hosts. While the warning exists, UserWarning is trivially suppressed and provides no protection. Users relying on this executor in production face real risk of data loss or system compromise. Marked P2 because it affects a specific code execution path rather than the core multi-agent orchestration.

source_issues.title: [Security] LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor executes LLM-generated code without sandboxing
source_issues.evidence: LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor writes LLM-generated code to disk and executes it without sandboxing. Only UserWarning at construction — easily suppressed. Severity: HIGH, OWASP ASI-09. Suggestion: upgrade to DeprecationWarning.

signals.topic: MultimodalWebSurfer agent vulnerable to indirect prompt injection via webpage title and URL
signals.summary: The MultimodalWebSurfer agent embeds attacker-controlled webpage metadata — specifically the title tag and URL — directly into LLM prompts without any sanitization or encoding. Malicious webpages can set a title containing injected instructions that are implicitly trusted by the agent, enabling indirect prompt injection attacks.
aliases: indirect prompt injection via title tag
signals.review_reason: Indirect prompt injection via untrusted webpage metadata is a well-established attack class. The WebSurfer agent is a core AutoGen capability for web browsing tasks; injecting malicious titles can manipulate agent behavior to exfiltrate data or perform unintended actions. While severity is rated MEDIUM, it directly undermines the trustworthiness of a primary agent capability. Marked P2 due to single-occurrence evidence.

source_issues.title: [Security] Web Surfer agent vulnerable to indirect prompt injection via page title
source_issues.evidence: MultimodalWebSurfer embeds attacker-controlled webpage metadata (title tag, URL) directly into LLM prompts without sanitization. Severity: MEDIUM, mapped to OWASP ASI-01. 10 comments indicating community interest.

signals.topic: Tool ID string length exceeds provider limit (41 > 40 chars) causing BadRequestError on Gemini-2.5 via litellm
signals.summary: When using vertex_ai/gemini-2.5-flash-preview-04-17 through litellm proxy, AutoGen generates tool call IDs with length 41, exceeding the provider's max length of 40, resulting in ContextWindowExceededError and BadRequestError. This is an interop bug that blocks API calls to specific LLM providers.
aliases: Gemini tool call id too long
signals.review_reason: Concrete interop bug with a full stack trace showing BadRequestError caused by AutoGen-generated tool ID length (41) exceeding the provider limit (40). This blocks API calls to Gemini-2.5 via litellm, a specific but real user scenario. Evidence is strong (reproducible with stack trace). Marked P2 due to single-occurrence count and narrow trigger condition (specific model via litellm proxy).

source_issues.title: Tool id string too long
source_issues.evidence: Tool id string too long (length 41, max 40) causing BadRequestError. Occurs when using vertex_ai/gemini-2.5-flash-preview-04-17 through litellm proxy. Stack trace shows ContextWindowExceededError due to tool call id string length.

signals.topic: Test discovery fails in VSCode Extension when code uses pure ESM packages
signals.summary: Playwright Test for VSCode Extension cannot discover tests when the project contains pure ESM packages with no CommonJS export, causing require() errors. Tests run fine from terminal but fail in VSCode test explorer.
aliases: require ES Module error in test explorer
signals.review_reason: Test discovery failure in VSCode IDE directly blocks the primary development workflow. Users lose IDE integration (test explorer, inline results) even though CLI execution still works, forcing a degraded debugging experience.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Playwright Test for VSCode Extension does not discover tests when pure ESM packages are used in code
source_issues.evidence: VSCode test explorer shows error 'require() of ES Module ... not supported' while the same tests execute successfully via npx from terminal. Main flow (test execution) blocked in VSCode IDE.

signals.topic: Video recording produces 0-byte files when page navigations occur between start and stop
signals.summary: playwright-cli video-start/video-stop produces 0-byte .webm files when multiple page navigations occur between start and stop. 100% reproducible, affects both headless and headed modes, and no workaround exists.
signals.review_reason: Core video recording feature produces completely invalid output. CI pipelines relying on video artifacts get empty files with no fallback. Confirmed 100% reproduction rate across multiple sessions and both browser modes.

source_issues.title: video-start/video-stop produces 0-byte files when navigations occur during recording
source_issues.evidence: 100% reproducible (5/5 independent sessions). output.webm is 0 bytes after multiple navigations. Single navigation works. Closing/reopening browser temporarily resets the issue. Blocks CI artifact generation.

signals.topic: Trace viewer fails to open traces larger than ~10MB due to Service Worker Response.blob() limitation
signals.summary: Playwright trace viewer (both local show-trace and trace.playwright.dev) cannot open traces from complex/long-running tests. Large .trace/.network files inside the zip trigger TypeError: Failed to fetch in Chromium Service Workers.
aliases: trace viewer TypeError Failed to fetch
trace zip open failure large files
signals.review_reason: Trace viewer is the primary debugging tool for Playwright test failures. When traces exceed ~10MB (common in complex E2E tests), the entire debug artifact becomes inaccessible, eliminating the main failure investigation workflow.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Trace viewer fails to open trace: Could not load trace from
source_issues.evidence: Console shows 'TypeError: Failed to fetch' and 'Could not load trace from ...zip' for large traces (>10MB). Simpler/smaller traces work fine. Primary debug artifact from test runs becomes inaccessible.

signals.topic: about:blank popup with document.write frameset — child frames invisible to Playwright in Chromium
signals.summary: When a page uses window.open('about:blank') followed by document.write() to build a frameset, Chromium returns only the main frame via page.frames(). Frameset children (menu, MainFrame, BlankFrame) are missing, causing waitForFrame() timeouts and all subsequent frame interactions to fail.
signals.review_reason: Frames created via about:blank + document.write frameset are invisible to Playwright's frame tree in Chromium, blocking all frame interaction for a common legacy application pattern. Workaround of using evaluate() is fragile and non-scalable.

source_issues.title: Bug Report: window.open('about:blank') popup with document.write() frameset not properly initialized in Chromium
source_issues.evidence: appPage.frames() returns only [''] in Chromium instead of expected ['', 'menu', 'MainFrame', 'BlankFrame']. waitForFrame() times out. All subsequent frame interactions fail. Blocks testing of legacy enterprise apps using this pattern.

signals.topic: Blank white page in headless mode after login — tests pass in headed mode but fail in CI
signals.summary: Tests that pass in headed mode consistently fail in headless mode with a blank white page appearing immediately after the login function executes. No error is thrown, making the failure silent and hard to debug.
signals.review_reason: Tests pass locally (headed) but fail silently in CI (headless) due to blank page rendering. This creates a critical CI/local parity gap where failures are only discoverable in production CI runs, making debugging expensive.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Blank White page in Headless mode of execution
source_issues.evidence: All tests pass in headed mode but fail in headless mode with a blank white page after login. This causes silent test failures in CI (headless by default) that are not reproducible locally. Screenshot shows white blank page.

signals.topic: Thinking/Reasoning mode fails across multiple AI connectors: Gemini thinking text leaks into user output, Bedrock thinking crashes after first tool call
signals.summary: Thinking mode is broken in two connectors: GoogleAI Gemini leaks internal reasoning text into the user-visible response, and Bedrock ChatClient crashes after the first tool call when thinking is enabled. Both break core agent functionality in common production scenarios.
aliases: Claude extended thinking breaks with tools
signals.review_reason: Thinking mode is a key capability for advanced reasoning. It is broken in two independent connectors across both Python and C# ecosystems — Gemini silently produces wrong output while Bedrock hard-crashes. Both prevent users from using this feature in real-world multi-agent scenarios where tools are essential.

source_issues.title: Python: Bug: Google AI connector leaks thinking/thought text parts into ChatMessageContent
source_issues.evidence: When Gemini thinking is enabled (include_thoughts=true), internal reasoning text (part.thought=True) leaks into the user-visible ChatMessageContent, replacing or mixing with the actual answer. Users see model thinking/reasoning text instead of actual responses.

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: Cannot enable thinking for BedrockChatClient with ChatClientAgent
source_issues.evidence: Enabling thinking via AdditionalProperties[thinking] on BedrockChatClient causes a crash after the first tool call when tools are enabled. The feature works without tools but is completely broken in the common agent-with-tools scenario.

signals.topic: PgVector connector crashes at runtime with Npgsql 10.0.2+ due to MissingMethodException
signals.summary: When Npgsql is upgraded to 10.0.2 (commonly via Entity Framework), the PgVector connector crashes with MissingMethodException on CollectionExistsAsync, making the entire vector search flow unusable and forcing a choice between EF upgrades and vector search.
aliases: vector store runtime crash with Npgsql upgrade
signals.review_reason: Runtime crash that makes the entire PgVector connector unusable. The common scenario of combining Entity Framework with PgVector triggers this crash, forcing users into a binary choice between EF upgrades and vector search capability — a clear main-flow failure with forced trade-off.

source_issues.title: Bug: System.MissingMethodException: 'Method not found: 'System.Threading.Tasks.Task Npgsql.NpgsqlConnection.ReloadTypesAsync()'.
source_issues.evidence: Runtime crash with MissingMethodException on CollectionExistsAsync() when Npgsql 10.0.2 is installed alongside PgVector. Users combining EF Core with PgVector are forced to either stay on Npgsql 8.x (blocking EF upgrades) or lose vector search functionality entirely.

signals.topic: MCPStreamableHttpPlugin hangs indefinitely on HTTP 401/403 during plugin initialization, blocking multi-agent tool use
signals.summary: When the MCP server returns HTTP 401 or 403 during plugin initialization, the plugin hangs forever because the error is trapped in a background task and never propagates. Applications wait until timeout (30s in PromptFlow), completely blocking MCP-based multi-agent workflows.
aliases: MCP plugin hangs on auth failure
signals.review_reason: The plugin enters an unbreakable hang state on auth failures, silently swallowing errors in a background task and surfacing only as a timeout. This completely blocks multi-agent workflows that rely on MCP tools, with no user-facing error message.

source_issues.title: Python: Bug: MCPStreamableHttpPlugin.__aenter__() method doesn't treat HTTP 401/403 as fatal errors
source_issues.evidence: connect() creates a background task that never sets ready_event when HTTP 401/403 occurs. The exception is trapped in the background task and never propagates, causing the application to hang until PromptFlow's 30-second timeout. Multi-agent workflows with MCP tools are completely blocked.

signals.topic: IAutoFunctionInvocationFilter context.Terminate=true corrupts ChatHistory, making all subsequent conversation turns fail with tool role errors
signals.summary: Using context.Terminate=true in an auto function invocation filter (common for call rate limiting) leaves ChatHistory in an inconsistent state. Every subsequent turn fails with 'messages with role tool must be a response to a preceding message with tool_calls', permanently breaking the conversation session.
aliases: tool role error after function call limit
AutoFunctionInvocationFilter terminates but leaves history broken
signals.review_reason: This bug permanently corrupts the ChatHistory state, making every subsequent conversation turn fail with a hard error. Users implementing function call rate limiting (a very common pattern) permanently break their conversation sessions — a session-level data integrity failure with no recovery path.

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: .Net: IAutoFunctionInvocationFilter - context.Terminate = true breaks ChatCompletion
source_issues.evidence: Setting context.Terminate=true in IAutoFunctionInvocationFilter (commonly used for function call rate limiting) leaves ChatHistory in an inconsistent state. All subsequent interactions fail with 'messages with role tool must be a response to a preceding message with tool_calls'. The entire conversation becomes permanently unusable after the limit is hit.

signals.topic: AgentGroupChat crashes when Azure Monitor telemetry is enabled due to unsupported dict-type response format in OpenTelemetry instrumentor
signals.summary: When Azure Monitor is configured via configure_azure_monitor, AgentGroupChat with AzureAIAgent fails with ValueError because the telemetry instrumentor does not support dict-type response_format. This blocks all multi-agent flows in telemetry-enabled production deployments.
aliases: OpenTelemetry instrumentor ValueError on dict format
signals.review_reason: A fundamental incompatibility between standard production telemetry setup (Azure Monitor/OpenTelemetry is standard in enterprise Azure deployments) and the agent execution pipeline. Users who enable observability lose all multi-agent functionality — this is a direct production-deployment blocker.

source_issues.title: Bug: [Python] AgentGroupChat fails with 'Unknown response format <class 'dict'>' when Azure Monitor is enabled
source_issues.evidence: The Azure AI OpenTelemetry instrumentor intercepts thread/run creation calls but does not support dict-type response_format values. All agent executions fail with ValueError when Azure Monitor is enabled. Automatic retries all fail identically, completely blocking multi-agent flows in telemetry-enabled production deployments.

signals.topic: MCP server initialization fails or produces incorrect results in 0.117.0, with errors hidden in default TUI path
signals.summary: Multiple MCP-related failures in 0.117.0: (a) MCP startup failures/warnings are hidden in the default app-server-backed TUI, making it appear Codex started cleanly when an MCP server actually failed; (b) chrome-devtools MCP server tools list shows '(none)' despite the server providing 25 tools.
signals.review_reason: Three distinct MCP failure modes: (1) startup errors silently suppressed in default TUI path, breaking health checks and diagnostics; (2) MCP tools list showing empty despite server providing 25 tools; (3) programmatic override 'mcp_servers={}' silently no-ops. MCP is a core extensibility feature — its failures block agent tool chains. Combined count=3, multiple manifestations, all with concrete repro steps and user impact.

source_issues.title: 0.117.0 regression: default tui_app_server hides MCP startup failures/warnings on startup
source_issues.evidence: Regression in 0.117.0 default path: MCP startup failures are completely hidden. With broken stdio MCP server, 'codex' reaches prompt with no error. 'codex --disable tui_app_server' shows: 'MCP client for example-stdio failed to start... MCP startup incomplete (failed: example-stdio)'. Startup-health checks and restart tooling will incorrectly conclude Codex started cleanly.

source_issues.title: 0.114.0 upgrade to 0.116.0/0.117.0 somewhat breaks MCP
source_issues.evidence: chrome-devtools MCP server configured correctly (nc 127.0.0.1:3333 provides 25 tools via direct nc test), but /mcp shows 'Tools: (none)' in 0.117.0. MCP tools list empty despite server working.

source_issues.title: bug: -c 'mcp_servers={}' silently no-ops instead of clearing MCP servers
source_issues.evidence: User intending to clear MCP servers for lightweight exec invocation uses -c 'mcp_servers={}' — appears to succeed but silently loads all servers anyway. Adds ~5K tokens of tool schemas and boot latency per call. Per-server disable workaround doesn't scale for programmatic CI use.

signals.topic: Auto-compaction/context compaction causes session hang, handoff output, or crash loop (regression in >=0.115)
signals.summary: After auto-compaction (`context_compacted`), Codex either emits a handoff/summary message and stops, or in headless exec mode compaction never fires at all, leading to context window overflow and a permanent crash loop. This breaks agent autonomy and blocks automated CI/agent workflows.
signals.review_reason: Two independent reports with strong evidence. #16042 shows regression in interactive mode with 2,620-session dataset (21/2620 repro rate, 3 complete session breaks). #16033 shows headless exec mode enters permanent crash loop after context overflow. Both are main-flow breaks — compaction is central to Codex's long-session operation, and its failure blocks the primary use case of Codex as an autonomous coding agent.

source_issues.title: Regression (>=0.115): after `context_compacted` auto-compaction Codex outputs handoff/summary and stops (CLI + Windows App)
source_issues.evidence: Regression from 0.115 onward. After context_compacted, Codex emits **Handoff/summary and ends turn. In 2,620 rollouts (16.6GB), 21 occurrences of context_compacted->handoff->task_complete found; 3/21 ended with no auto-continue requiring manual resume. A/B confirmed: 0.114.0 safe, 0.117.0 reproduces immediately.

source_issues.title: Auto-compaction never triggers in headless exec mode (codex exec), context overflow crash loop
source_issues.evidence: Auto-compaction never fires in headless exec mode. 86 shell commands (~242K tokens) accumulated with zero compact events. Session crashes at context window limit. Watcher retries, each retry adds to session → permanent crash loop. Token tracking reports empty in exec mode. Blocks automated agent workflows reading large codebases.

signals.topic: Codex consumes token quota at extremely high/unexpected rates, rendering the service unusable for Pro/Plus users
signals.summary: Pro and Plus users observe catastrophic token consumption even for minimal usage (e.g., 'Hi' prompt draining 63% of daily quota). The root cause traced to plugin system in 0.117.0 — disabling plugins restores normal consumption.
signals.review_reason: Two users on Pro and Plus tiers both experiencing extreme/quasi-catastrophic token drain in 0.117.0, one explicitly stating Codex becomes 'unusable'. The 0.117.0 plugin system is identified as the root cause. This is a direct cost impact for paying users — the core value proposition (affordable coding assistance) is negated when quota is exhausted by trivial usage.

source_issues.title: Unbelievable sudden token usage
source_issues.evidence: Pro user reports ~63% of daily token quota consumed with very conservative usage, after reset. 'After the reset this morning, and clearly much much lower usage as shown in my usage chart. This is clearly a very extreme bug. This is going to make codex unusable for me.'

source_issues.title: Codex Drains Token Quota and Context Window at Startup with Simple 'Hi' Prompt
source_issues.evidence: Plus user: simple 'Hi' prompt consumes ~15% of context window on every session start in 0.117.0. Sending 'Hi' five times dropped remaining quota to ~37%. Disabling all plugins restores normal ~2-3% per first prompt. Root cause traced to plugin system.

signals.topic: Regression in 0.117.0: /copy command fails with 'unavailable before first Codex output' error after Codex has already produced output
signals.summary: /copy command incorrectly reports 'unavailable before the first Codex output' even when Codex has already responded. Downgrade to 0.116.0 resolves it, confirming this is a regression.
signals.review_reason: Clear regression with A/B confirmation (0.116.0 vs 0.117.0 on same machine). /copy is a documented user-facing command that breaks after the first Codex response. While count=1, the evidence quality is high (explicit downgrade/upgrade A/B test) and it represents a user-facing feature regression in a recent release affecting all platforms.

source_issues.title: Regression: /copy fails in 0.117.0 after first Codex output in a normal session
source_issues.evidence: Reproduced on same machine: downgrade to 0.116.0 → /copy works; upgrade to 0.117.0 → /copy fails with error '/copy is unavailable before the first Codex output or right after a rollback'. A/B testing confirms regression. Key UX command fails post first output in normal sessions.

signals.topic: Concurrent `codex mcp remove` operations silently lose config updates in ~/.codex/config.toml
signals.summary: Parallel `codex mcp remove` commands report success but leave some MCP entries in config.toml due to no cross-process locking. Final config state is indeterminate.
signals.review_reason: Race condition in config mutation is a data-integrity issue. The CLI reports success while silently losing some updates — users cannot trust the output. Detailed repro script with isolated HOME confirms. While count=1, the defect is deterministic and reproducible, with clear user impact: batch cleanup operations silently fail.

source_issues.title: Concurrent `codex mcp remove` silently loses updates in ~/.codex/config.toml
source_issues.evidence: Four parallel 'codex mcp remove' commands each report 'Removed global MCP server' but final config.toml still contains some of the target entries. Repro via disposable HOME with isolated config. Sequential execution works correctly. CLI reports success while data is silently lost.

signals.topic: Base64 image_url type rejected by completion API when using chat_completions mode
signals.summary: Agents SDK only accepts 'input_image' type for image inputs but completion API (chat_completions mode) requires 'image_url'. Requests silently fail to reach the user's Azure OpenAI endpoint, causing main workflow blockage with no error indication.
aliases: image_url vs input_image type mismatch in completion API mode
signals.review_reason: Main workflow is blocked: user cannot use base64 image inputs with Azure OpenAI via completion API. The SDK silently drops the request, forcing users to use workarounds that don't actually work.

source_issues.title: Error when sending base64 img to GPT-4.1(not supporting completion api)
source_issues.evidence: User reports SDK rejects image_url type in chat_completions mode, request never reaches Azure endpoint. Changing to input_image makes request go through but breaks at Azure side since completion API doesn't support it.

signals.topic: Prompt caching drops to 0% when base64 file inputs are introduced, causing significant cost increase
signals.summary: Adding file inputs (base64-encoded) causes cache hit rate to drop from ~96% to 0%, even when prompt prefix, system instructions, and tool definitions remain unchanged. This leads to repeated high token costs for multi-turn conversations with file inputs.
aliases: prompt cache hit drops to 0% when file inputs are used
cache efficiency collapses with mixed text and file input requests
signals.review_reason: Direct cost impact: cache efficiency dropping from 96% to 0% means every request after a file input round pays full token cost. For production multi-turn agents, this represents significant unexpected cost with no user control.

source_issues.title: Prompt caching drops to 0% when introducing base64 file inputs
source_issues.evidence: User reports consistent cache drop from 96.7% to 0% when file inputs are introduced in round 3, even though prefix, instructions, and tool definitions are unchanged. Cost impact is significant for production workloads relying on caching.

signals.topic: griffe/griffelib version conflict causes ImportError crash in CI and service environments
signals.summary: When both griffe 1.15.0 and griffelib 2.0.0 are installed (e.g., by uv), they overwrite each other's entry points, causing ImportError: cannot import name 'ExprInterpolation'. This crashes agents/tool.py initialization in CI pipelines and deployed services.
signals.review_reason: Service startup crash: agents/tool.py fails to import due to griffe/griffelib conflict, blocking entire service from starting in CI and deployed environments.

source_issues.title: maybe use griffelib instead of griffe as dependency, and update to 2+
source_issues.evidence: User reports CI and service crash with ImportError when both griffe 1.15.0 and griffelib 2.0.0 are present. Stack trace shows failure in agents/tool.py import chain. Crashes on startup.

signals.topic: ToolCallItem title and description fields are lost during session persistence round-trip
signals.summary: When ToolCallItem is serialized via to_input_item() during session persistence, the title and description fields (added in recent SDK versions) are dropped because the base RunItemBase.to_input_item() uses model_dump(exclude_unset=True). This breaks session history for multi-turn agent conversations using handoffs.
aliases: to_input_item() drops SDK-local fields on serialization
signals.review_reason: Session persistence silently drops metadata fields, causing title and description to be lost across conversation history. This breaks agent handoff workflows and any downstream system relying on complete session state.

source_issues.title: ToolCallItem.to_input_item() drops title and description on session persistence
source_issues.evidence: User provides minimal repro showing 'title' and 'description' are absent from to_input_item() output. Specific code path identified: save_result_to_session -> run_item_to_input_item -> to_input_item() uses model_dump which excludes unset fields.

signals.topic: Guardrail follow-up races with response.cancel causing 'Conversation already has an active response' error in realtime mode
signals.summary: In realtime mode with turn detection enabled, the guardrail sends response.cancel then immediately sends response.create for the follow-up. If the cancel hasn't completed (response.done not received), the create call fails with 'Conversation already has an active response in progress'. Reproducible under network latency.
aliases: response.cancel and response.create race in guardrail
signals.review_reason: Realtime workflow is intermittently broken: guardrail interruption fails with active response error under network latency conditions. This is a race condition that blocks realtime agent use cases.

source_issues.title: Guardrail follow-up can race with response.cancel completion
source_issues.evidence: User reports 'Conversation already has an active response in progress' error during realtime guardrail flow. Root cause identified: no wait for response.done between interrupt and follow-up in session.py L956-964. Commenter on related issue also hit same error after upgrading to 0.4.1.

signals.topic: Responses API multi-turn conversations fail on turn 2 (model_dump null fabrication + undocumented pairing constraint)
signals.summary: Two interrelated bugs block the fundamental multi-turn conversation pattern: (1) model_dump() fabricates null fields (status: None, encrypted_content: None) causing 400 'Unknown parameter', and (2) an undocumented constraint requires reasoning+message items to appear as consecutive pairs — the common pattern of filtering response.output to only messages silently orphans reasoning items and 400s. OpenClaw (64.9k forks) has confirmed production breakage. Affects Python, JS, Go, Java, .NET SDKs. Root cause is shared (API spec openai/openai-openapi#536).
signals.review_reason: Both issues are the primary blocker for the Responses API's multi-turn conversation use case — the most fundamental workflow. Confirmed production breakage at OpenClaw (64.9k forks). Cross-SDK impact across 5+ repos. Despite count=2 (below the ≥3 heuristic), the user impact is severe and unambiguous: the core multi-turn pattern is broken, with no reliable workaround except previous_response_id (which is not equivalent).

signals.topic: jiter corrupts tool call arguments by converting escaped double-quotes to single-quotes
signals.summary: The jiter dependency converts escaped double-quotes (\" in JSON) to escaped single-quotes (\') during deserialization, producing invalid JSON that cannot be parsed by json.loads(). This breaks ALL tool/function calling with multi-field arguments for any application using the OpenAI Python SDK with OpenAI-compatible servers (llama.cpp, vLLM, Ollama). Particularly impacts the Home Assistant ecosystem where multiple integrations depend on the SDK for smart home device control.
aliases: escaped quotes converted to single quotes
signals.review_reason: Blocks core tool-calling functionality for any multi-field tool call. Root cause is definitively in the SDK's jiter deserialization layer — confirmed by comparing raw HTTP (correct) vs SDK output (corrupted). Workaround requires manual string replacement before json.loads(), which is fragile and non-obvious.

source_issues.title: Tool call arguments field has escaped double-quotes converted to single-quotes by jiter
source_issues.evidence: Raw HTTP response has correct escaped JSON (\"domain\": \"climate\") but SDK tc.function.arguments returns corrupted '{"name": "Master Bedroom AC\', domain: \'climate"}'. json.loads() fails. Reproduces on stream and non-stream. Affects Home Assistant ecosystem integrations with local LLM servers.

signals.topic: Batch API result file download fails with ConnectionResetError for large outputs (>200MB)
signals.summary: Downloading Batch API result files exceeding ~200-300MB (e.g., 50k embedding rows) causes httpcore.RemoteProtocolError: peer closed connection without sending complete message body. Users must manually implement chunked download with exponential backoff as a workaround. Prevents large-scale batch processing workflows from completing.
signals.review_reason: Blocks large-scale batch processing workflows. The connection is dropped mid-download for files >200MB, and the issue affects all download approaches (SDK streaming, requests library, all timeout configurations). Users are forced into manual chunking workarounds, which is not a viable solution for production batch pipelines.

Workaround: split into 10k batches (~200MB files). Confirmed reproducible with SDK streaming, direct requests library, and requests with timeout=(10, 300).

signals.topic: prompt_cache_retention SDK type uses 'in-memory' (hyphen) but API expects 'in_memory' (underscore)
signals.summary: The SDK declares prompt_cache_retention with Literal['in-memory', '24h'] (hyphen) across Responses API, Chat Completions, and Response model types. The API rejects 'in-memory' with 400 Bad Request and only accepts 'in_memory' (underscore). Users must add # type: ignore to bypass the type checker, making the feature unusable without workarounds.

source_issues.evidence: API 400 Bad Request when using SDK-typed value 'in-memory'. Requires # type: ignore workaround to use correct 'in_memory' value. Bug present in three locations: ResponseCreateParams, CompletionCreateParams, and Response model.

signals.topic: AsyncStream lacks aclose() async cleanup method, causing AttributeError in instrumented async workflows
signals.summary: AsyncStream exposes close() but not aclose(), violating the standard Python async cleanup convention (PEP 525). When instrumentation libraries like Langfuse wrap AsyncStream, calling __aexit__ triggers a call chain that resolves .response to the AsyncStream itself, causing AttributeError. This breaks LangChain + Langfuse + structured output streaming in production.
signals.review_reason: Causes AttributeError crashes in production async workflows using popular instrumentation tools (Langfuse) and frameworks (LangChain). While it requires a specific chain (instrumentation + streaming + structured output), the failure is a hard crash that prevents graceful async cleanup, and the pattern is likely to spread as more tools add async instrumentation.

source_issues.title: AsyncStream missing aclose() causes AttributeError in streaming structured output
source_issues.evidence: AttributeError: 'AsyncStream' object has no attribute 'aclose'. Full traceback through AsyncChatCompletionStreamManager.__aexit__ → stream.close() → _response.aclose(). Triggered by Langfuse 3.11.2+ instrumentation wrapping OpenAI streaming responses in LangChain with structured output.

signals.topic: All `ruflo memory` subcommands hang indefinitely after completion — ONNX worker threads prevent Node.js exit
signals.summary: Every memory subcommand (init, stats, store, search, list, cleanup, compress) hangs forever after completing work. Root cause: ONNX embedding model workers keep the Node.js event loop alive with no `process.exit()` in the CLI entry point. Two independent reports confirm the issue.
signals.review_reason: Memory subcommands (all of them) hang indefinitely after completing work on every platform. This is a main flow failure — the core memory feature cannot be used without manually killing the process. Two independent reports confirm ONNX worker threads prevent natural process exit. PR #1441 was opened to fix it, confirming the root cause is in the codebase.

source_issues.title: memory init hangs after completion — process does not exit (ONNX worker threads not terminated)
source_issues.evidence: On Windows, `npx ruflo memory init` completes successfully (prints 'Synced to: memory.db') but never exits. Process must be Ctrl+C'd. Root cause: ONNX Runtime spawns worker threads that are never terminated. Also observed: ONNX model loaded twice, broken dependency path, 1 of 5 AgentDB controllers failed.

source_issues.title: fix: ruflo memory subcommands hang after completion — process.exit() missing from CLI entry point
source_issues.evidence: All memory subcommands hang after completing their work. Root cause: `ensureInitialized()` in memory-tools.ts loads ONNX model which spawns worker threads that are never terminated. CLI entry point `bin/cli.js` only calls `process.exit(1)` on error, not `process.exit(0)` on success. Fix implemented in PR #1441.

signals.topic: Headless daemon workers fail 100% on Windows — daemon crashes on startup and headless workers return empty output

signals.review_reason: Multiple independent root causes all block the same core feature on Windows. Daemon crashes (path with spaces), premature exit (missing keepalive), and empty worker output (broken IPC) together make the entire token optimization feature unusable on Windows. source_issues.title: Windows: Daemon headless workers return empty output, breaking token optimization

When daemon IS running, headless workers spawn `claude --print` via stdin pipe but stdout is empty on Windows — the core token optimization is completely broken. Model routing, AgentBooster, and all daemon-scheduled workers (audit, optimize, testgaps) are non-functional. Local patches required after every npm cache clean.

All 3 workers fail 100% with 'There's an issue with the selected model' error. Each failed run takes ~89 seconds. Daemon running since Mar 24: 55 audit runs (9 fails), 40 optimize (7 fails), 25 testgaps (5 fails) — all recent runs failing since model IDs expired.

signals.topic: Spawned agents (reviewer, security-architect, tester) complete work but have no results endpoint — fire-and-forget only
signals.summary: `agent_spawn` creates agents that complete their work, but `agent_status` returns no results field and there is no `agent_results` endpoint. The alternative WASM agents fail with a missing package error. Reviewer/security agents are effectively unusable in CI workflows.
signals.review_reason: Multi-agent orchestration's core promise is that spawned agents produce actionable output. The current implementation only provides metadata tracking — agents run to completion but their findings are inaccessible. This is a main flow failure for the agent spawning feature, blocking CI-style workflows that need to report findings back to users. The WASM fallback also fails with a missing package, leaving no working alternative.

source_issues.title: agent_spawn results not retrievable — no way to get agent output after completion
source_issues.evidence: `agent_status` returns '{"status": "idle", "taskCount": 0}' with no results field. No `agent_results` or `agent_output` endpoint exists. Spawned reviewer/security-architect agents complete work but output cannot be retrieved. WASM alternative also fails: 'Cannot find package @ruvector/rvagent-wasm'. Agents are fire-and-forget, unusable in CI workflows that need to report findings.

signals.topic: Daemon startup hangs/fails across multiple platforms — no usable CLI on Linux VMs, Windows 11, and Linux Servers
signals.summary: On Ubuntu 24.04 LTS VMs, Windows 11, and Linux Server/NAS environments, the daemon fails to start or hangs silently, causing the entire CLI to be unusable with OS-level errors (os error 11, os error 10013, os error 2).
aliases: daemon fails to start on Linux VM
daemon fails to start Windows 11 TCP bind
daemon fails to start Linux Server NAS
signals.review_reason: Three independent reports from three different OS environments (Ubuntu 24.04 VM, Windows 11, Linux Server/NAS) all show the same root failure: daemon never starts or hangs, making agent-browser entirely unusable. This is a main-process blocker — no command works without a running daemon. Strong user impact confirmed across all three reports with concrete OS-level error codes and reproducible steps.

source_issues.title: CLI hangs and throws os error 11 (Resource temporarily unavailable) on Ubuntu 24.04 VM
source_issues.evidence: CLI hangs without response, times out with 'Failed to read: Resource temporarily unavailable (os error 11) (after 5 retries - daemon may be busy or unresponsive)'. Chrome process never even starts. No socket file created.

source_issues.title: Daemon fails to start on Windows 11: TCP bind permission denied (os error 10013) and unclear which port is being used
source_issues.evidence: Daemon exits during startup with 'Failed to bind TCP: os error 10013'. Error message does not specify which port, making diagnosis impossible. Occurs even with Administrator privileges.

source_issues.title: agent-browser open hangs on Linux Server/NAS - daemon fails to start (OpenClaw agent)
source_issues.evidence: CLI hangs indefinitely with no output. No socket file created at ~/.agent-browser/. Chrome process never starts. Error 'No such file or directory (os error 2) after 5 retries'. Running in OpenClaw AI agent on Linux Server/NAS environment.

signals.topic: CDP connect hangs indefinitely when browser has discarded/frozen tabs (Memory Saver enabled)
signals.summary: When connecting via --cdp to a browser with Memory Saver enabled, the daemon hangs forever because Page.enable sent to discarded tabs never responds. Their renderer processes were killed to save memory. This affects the majority of real-world CDP users.
aliases: CDP connection hangs with Memory Saver
signals.review_reason: Despite count=1, this is a main-workflow blocker for the majority of CDP users: 70% of tabs in typical browser sessions are discarded by Memory Saver, making this affect most real-world CDP connection attempts. The hang is indefinite with no timeout or error message. Confirmed reproducible with 20-tab test on both Brave and Chrome. Root cause identified in browser.rs discover_and_attach_targets().

source_issues.title: Bug: CDP connect hangs on browsers with discarded/frozen tabs (Memory Saver)
source_issues.evidence: 14 out of 20 randomly sampled tabs were discarded and timed out on Page.enable. After disabling Memory Saver, 5/5 tabs responded instantly. The daemon hangs forever on the first discarded tab — no timeout, no error, no recovery. Root cause: discover_and_attach_targets() attaches all page targets including discarded ones whose renderer processes were killed.

signals.topic: Chrome crash leaves zombie process — daemon hangs indefinitely with no auto-restart or error
signals.summary: When Chrome crashes (SIGTRAP/CHECK() failure), the daemon does not call waitpid() to reap the zombie process, does not restart Chrome, and hangs silently on all subsequent commands with no timeout or error.
signals.review_reason: Main workflow blocking: any Chrome crash (common in headless automation) renders the daemon permanently non-functional with no timeout and no error. The user has no indication the daemon is dead and no way to recover except manual process killing. Root cause is identified (no SIGCHLD handling, no waitpid(), no restart logic). Confirmed reproducible with kill -TRAP reproduction steps. Severity is high — automated pipelines using agent-browser will silently fail after any Chrome instability.

source_issues.title: Daemon hangs indefinitely after Chrome crash: zombie process not reaped, no auto-restart
source_issues.evidence: Chrome becomes [chrome] <defunct> (zombie). Daemon stays alive but non-functional. All subsequent CLI commands hang indefinitely with no timeout and no error. Only recovery: kill -9 <daemon-pid>. Root cause: no SIGCHLD handler, no waitpid() call, no restart logic. Confirmed on both v0.22.2 and v0.21.4.

signals.topic: tab list does not show tabs opened after --cdp connection (regression in v0.20.0 Rust rewrite)
signals.summary: When connecting via --cdp, tab list only shows tabs present at connection time. Any tab opened afterward is invisible. This is a confirmed regression from v0.20.0; v0.19.0 correctly tracked new tabs via context.on('page', ...).
aliases: new tabs not visible after CDP connect
signals.review_reason: Core CDP workflow is broken: users cannot see tabs opened after connecting to their browser. Clear regression from v0.20.0 confirmed by comparing behavior against v0.19.0. Root cause is identified in two places: browser.rs filtering newtab as internal target AND daemon.rs not processing events between commands. While count=1, the regression is confirmed and the workflow is blocked.

source_issues.title: tab list does not show tabs opened after --cdp connection
source_issues.evidence: Regression from v0.20.0. v0.19.0 correctly shows new tabs via context.on('page', ...). v0.22.3 silently drops Target.targetCreated events because the background drain loop only runs when request_tracking || har_recording is active, and the event channel overflow error is swallowed. Root cause identified in browser.rs plus daemon.rs.

signals.topic: snapshot -i output format changed in v0.22.1 Rust daemon — breaking change for data.refs consumers
signals.summary: The snapshot -i command in v0.22.1 produces a different JSON structure than v0.19.0. The data.refs dictionary is missing on complex pages (forms with radio buttons), breaking automation pipelines that depend on programmatic element extraction.
aliases: snapshot JSON structure changed breaking change
signals.review_reason: Breaking change from the v0.20.0 Rust rewrite that forces users to pin to v0.19.0 and blocks upgrades. The data.refs JSON output is used programmatically by automation pipelines — when it disappears on complex pages, the system falls back to LLM hallucination instead of reliable element extraction. Clear production impact documented with specific page URL and element counts.

source_issues.title: Bug: `snapshot -i` output format changed in v0.22.1 (Rust daemon) — breaks structured `data.refs` parsing
source_issues.evidence: On form pages with radio buttons, v0.22.1 returns 0 refs vs. 3 in v0.19.0. Automation pipeline falls back to LLM which hallucinates form options. Users are pinned to v0.19.0 and cannot upgrade. Impact confirmed on real production pipeline with public test URL.

signals.topic: Rule 2.1 (Avoid Barrel Imports) 与 lucide-react 直接导入路径不提供 .d.ts 类型声明，导致 TypeScript "implicit any" 错误
signals.summary: react-best-practices 规则建议使用直接路径导入以提升开发性能，但 lucide-react 的直接路径仅提供 .js 文件而无对应 .d.ts，导致 AI agent 遵循规则后引入 TypeScript 类型错误，需要人工干预或全局声明文件 workaround
aliases: barrel import rule conflicts with type definitions
signals.review_reason: 有明确用户影响证据：Rule 2.1 应用于 lucide-react 时会导致 TypeScript 'implicit any' 错误，破坏代码类型安全，需要人工干预修复，构成真实的体验降级。但因 count=1、仅单仓问题，归为 P2。

source_issues.title: `react-best-practices` Rule 2.1 (Avoid Barrel Imports) creates TypeScript "any" type errors with lucide-react
source_issues.evidence: 用户报告 AI agent 遵循 Rule 2.1 直接导入 lucide-react 图标时，TypeScript 报 'implicit any' 错误，需要手动干预或添加 declarations.d.ts workaround。规则本身在性能与类型安全之间产生冲突。

signals.topic: streamText parsePartialOutput causes quadratic O(n) string copies leading to OOM kills in production
signals.summary: streamText with default text() output calls JSON.stringify on accumulated text for every chunk, creating N full-length string copies. With concurrent streams on long outputs, heap grows to 3.4GB causing OOM on 4GB containers. Root cause: text() output always returns non-undefined from parsePartialOutput, triggering JSON.stringify even when no structured output is needed. Fix is a one-line change (return undefined in parsePartialOutput for text output).
signals.review_reason: Confirmed production OOM kills on containers with concurrent long-output streams. Heap snapshots show 1.6GB of retained string objects from JSON.stringify inside createOutputTransformStream. This is a main-flow failure (streaming breaks entirely under memory pressure) with direct cost impact (container crashes, OOM restarts). Workaround exists but requires users to fork the default text() output. High severity despite count=1 due to multiplicative concurrency impact and clear root cause.

source_issues.title: streamText Memory Issue: parsePartialOutput creates O(n) string copies
source_issues.evidence: Production OOM kills confirmed; 3 concurrent streams produce ~1.6GB of string copies in large_object_space; 25x memory reduction measured after fix; affects all plain-text streamText users on Node.js with long outputs

signals.topic: isDynamicToolUIPart function not exported in SDK index.ts despite being in source and documented
signals.summary: The isDynamicToolUIPart function exists in the SDK source code but is not exported from the package's public index.ts, making it inaccessible to users. The function is referenced in official documentation, so users following docs are blocked from using the feature.
signals.review_reason: Key documented feature is completely inaccessible because the function is not exported. This is a packaging/release defect that directly blocks users from using advertised functionality. While count=1, the impact is clear (docs reference it, users can't use it) and the fix is trivial (add to exports).

source_issues.title: bug: is `isDynamicToolUIPart` is not exported in index.ts
source_issues.evidence: Function exists in source (packages/ai/src/ui/index.ts and packages/ai/src/ui/ui-messages.ts) but not exported. Referenced in official docs, users following docs are blocked.

signals.topic: @ai-sdk/open-responses silently drops non-image file parts (e.g., PDF) from requests
signals.summary: When using generateText with @ai-sdk/open-responses provider, file parts with non-image media types (e.g., application/pdf) are silently dropped. The SDK logs a warning but sends the request without the file data. The model then responds that no document was provided, causing request failure that is hard to diagnose.
aliases: unsupported file content type silent drop
signals.review_reason: Silent data loss: user-attached files are dropped without throwing an error, causing the model to receive a different request than intended. The warning is easy to miss in production logs, leading to confusing model behavior. This directly breaks document processing workflows that users expect to work. Root cause is a 2-line hardcoded check in the SDK.

source_issues.title: @ai-sdk/open-responses drops non-image file parts (e.g., PDF)
source_issues.evidence: Hardcoded check in convertToOpenResponsesInput rejects non-image files with warning 'unsupported file content type'. Request sent without file data; model responds 'no document provided'. Full reproduction with PDF included in issue. OpenAI Responses API supports non-image files via input_file part.

signals.topic: resume:true triggers N resume-stream requests when useChat is used across multiple shared-context components
signals.summary: When a Chat instance is held in a shared React context and used by multiple components via useChat({ chat }), each component instance independently triggers a resume-stream request. With 20+ components using the pattern, 20+ duplicate resume requests fire instead of 1. This causes significant unnecessary API traffic and potential rate limiting issues.
aliases: useChat shared context duplicate resume requests
resume stream fires multiple times shared context
signals.review_reason: Duplicate resume-stream requests cause unnecessary API calls, potential rate limiting, and wasted compute. The pattern (shared context + multiple useChat consumers) is explicitly documented by Vercel in their official cookbook, making this a scenario users are expected to use. With 20+ components, this could mean 20x the expected API load. P2 rather than P1 because it does not block the main flow — it causes resource waste and potential downstream rate limit errors rather than complete failure.

source_issues.title: Resume:true triggers resume-stream request for every usage of useChat when Chat is in shared context
source_issues.evidence: App with 20+ components using useChat({ chat }) pattern with shared ChatContext triggers 20+ resume-stream requests instead of 1. Heap snapshot screenshot provided. Related to React StrictMode (which doubles to 40+). Described as 'not ideal' in related PR but escalated because multi-component use case makes it a disaster.

signals.topic: @ai-sdk/xai responses streaming silently drops final text fragments when content block already exists
signals.summary: In @ai-sdk/xai Responses streaming path, the doStream handler only emits text-delta when a content block does not already exist. When a block already exists, subsequent contentPart.text fragments are silently ignored, causing output truncation. The final text is permanently lost from the stream with no error or indication.
aliases: xai response stream drops final text
text-delta not emitted for existing content block xai
signals.review_reason: Silent output truncation: final text fragments are permanently lost from the stream with no error, no exception, and no indication to the user. The stream appears to complete normally (finish: stop, no error) but the output is incomplete. This breaks any downstream processing that relies on complete streamed output (display, storage, parsing). The bug is in the xAI provider's streaming handler and has a clear, validated fix.

source_issues.title: @ai-sdk/xai responses stream drops final text fragments in doStream when content block already exists
source_issues.evidence: Output truncation confirmed with long deterministic prompts. Final marker 'END_OK_9981' missing from output. Truncated text already persisted in streamed output before it was cut off. Fix validated: moving text-delta outside the block creation condition restores full output. Root cause is conditional that skips text-delta emission when block already exists.

signals.topic: Turbopack barrel import optimization causes runtime undefined component crash in monorepo production builds
signals.summary: When mixing barrel imports and direct sub-path imports of the same module under Turbopack, the direct import path's chunk dependencies are not correctly tracked, causing components to be undefined at runtime. Crashes React with error #130.
aliases: Turbopack barrel optimization chunk dependency bug
mixed barrel and direct imports undefined component
signals.review_reason: Runtime crash in production (React error #130, element type invalid). Causes complete component failure visible to end users. Count=2, Turbopack is the default bundler for next dev, and the workaround (unifying all imports to barrel style) is non-obvious and fragile in large monorepos.

source_issues.title: Turbopack: mixing direct and barrel imports of the same module causes undefined component at runtime
source_issues.evidence: Overline is undefined at runtime → React error #130. Module chunk dependency not correctly tracked when both barrel and direct import paths coexist. Works through barrel import path but fails through direct import path.

source_issues.title: Turbopack: mixing direct and barrel imports of the same module causes undefined component at runtime
source_issues.evidence: Identical root cause as #91927. Direct import path module 663281 defined in a different chunk than consuming component, with missing chunk dependency declarations.

signals.topic: Client Component onClick events fail to fire on iOS Safari in Next.js 16.2.1 (regression from 16.1.6)

Client Component onClick broken on iOS 16.2.1

Count=1 but the user impact is severe and widespread across all iOS mobile users, meeting P0 threshold through review_reason evidence.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Client Component onClick events fail to fire on iOS Safari (Next.js 16.2.1)
source_issues.evidence: Button with onClick handler in a Client Component does not trigger state update on iOS Safari. Confirmed regression: downgrading to 16.1.6 immediately resolves the issue. Affects mobile-first development severely — same code works on desktop browsers and on Next.js 15.

signals.topic: manifest.ts file breaks Hot Module Replacement (HMR) in Next.js 16.2
signals.summary: Using a manifest.ts file in Next.js 16.2 causes HMR to stop triggering. UI does not update after code changes. Even a hard reload does not reflect changes. Only resolves after deleting the .next build folder.
signals.review_reason: Severely blocks the primary developer workflow (hot reloading during development). Every code change requires deleting .next and restarting the dev server, completely breaking the iterative development loop. Affects all Next.js 16.2 users who use manifest.ts (a core App Router feature). Count=1 but experience impact is developer-flow-blocking, meeting P0 threshold.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: manifest.ts breaks HMR in Next.js 16.2
source_issues.evidence: HMR does not trigger after code changes with manifest.ts present. Hard reload (Cmd+Shift+R) does not reflect latest changes. Changes only appear after deleting .next build folder and restarting. Issue did not occur before 16.2, still present in latest canary 16.2.1-canary.10.

signals.topic: router.push triggers full page reload instead of soft navigation with output:'export' static export in 16.2.1 (regression from 16.1.6)

aliases: static export router.push full reload regression 16.2.1
output export router.push MPA instead of soft navigation
signals.review_reason: Regression in 16.2.1 blocking static site generation (SSG) production deployments. Full page reload causes JavaScript state loss and broken SPA experience. The issue has clear reproduction steps, concrete evidence (beforeunload fires, history.pushState not called), and is confirmed absent in 16.1.6. Labeled 'invalid link' but the underlying bug evidence is thorough.

source_issues.title: router.push triggers full page reload instead of soft navigation with output: 'export' in Next.js 16.2.1

All subsequent navigations work correctly. Does not occur in next dev mode.

signals.topic: create-next-app pnpm version detection incorrectly omits packages field for pnpm >= 10.4.1, causing 'packages field missing or empty' error
signals.summary: create-next-app generates a pnpm-workspace.yaml that omits the packages field for all pnpm versions >= 10, causing pnpm install to fail with 'packages field missing or empty' for pnpm versions 10.4.1 through 10.4.x.
signals.review_reason: Blocks new project creation for users with pnpm 10.4.x (a currently common version). create-next-app is the primary entry point for new Next.js users. The root cause is identified in source code, making it a clear and fixable bug.

source_issues.title: Can't PNPM Install using pnpm version 10 < x < 10.5.0
source_issues.evidence: pnpm i produces 'packages field missing or empty' error when using create-next-app with pnpm 10.4.1. Root cause identified in source code: packages prop omitted for all pnpm versions after 10, but should only be omitted for specific versions. Blocks new project creation.

signals.topic: getTeamMembers API requires teamId but SDK does not accept the parameter

signals.topic: CLI deployment of Turbo monorepo apps with internal workspace packages fails (npm 404 on internal packages)
